commit message:
Updated exercise 4

This commit updates exercise 4. Parts where solutions are found from R demos are removed, and
parts about computing MCSEs are added. Rubric is also updated. No longer needed functions
and markmyassignment tests are removed.

This commit also adds the mcse_quantile function to the aaltobda package.
This function is used in the exercise to compute MCSE of quantiles for independent draws.
The function is a simplified version of a similar function from the loo package,
but now instead of effective samples size, the actual sample size is used.

between the original and new clustering code and verifies that they're the

implemented in the snn_helper and snn_vectorized files but will be deleted in the

commit message:
add additional tests for CDEs

cde_behavior_test is the start of a test suite for ML behavioral
testing. Right now, the only test it contains checks that the training
loss goes down over time for each CDE.

cde_regression_test compares the output of the CDE to a saved, "correct"
result. Since the results of the CDEs are pretty variable, this test
calculates the mean for each feature from the CDE output, and checks
that they are equal between arrays within a 15% relative tolerance (see numpy
allclose for details on what that means).

author: Josh Lurz <jlurz24@gmail.com>
commit message:
Code reworked to use the Matrix Template Library instead of gaussj subroutine. In testing produced nearly the exact same results. Will require the installation of the MTL, located in a zip file in the shared directory above the code(mtl.zip). Simply unzip the file and add the path to your IDE. Use this version instead of the one on the website, it includes a small bugfix I made.

The new code should have several advantages:
easier to understand.
uses an LU factorization to inverse the matrix which should be faster theoretically than the trisolve algorithm.
puts us in better legal standing.
much better memory usage.
allows for more future capabilities.

author: Steven J Smith <ssmith@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
I just committed my newest code.  Below is my CVS comment I put in the log.
Note the note about calibration at the end. I also put in a check for zero
priceElas in subresources (which was causing a problem with nuclear), there
aren't any others.


Implemented smooth function for the change in share due to a capacity limit.
Implemented capacity limits for demand sectors.
Turned off calibrations during bracketing (code solves faster and helps calibration).

Added back base-year calibrations for demand sectors in reference.xml.
Added non-energy use oil sub-sector in reference.xml (emits no CO2).
Changed nuclear energy calibration from input to output so that is independent of efficiency assumption.

Because calibrations are turned off during NR solver, code does not calibrate exactly. Seems to be largely a problem for TFE in later years. One way to solve this is to add a call to bisection and then NR (this could use the same derivatives) after the initial solution. It may also be that a call to NR with the same derivatives, but with calibration turned on, would also work. In either case, should be able to do this with only a small increase in model run-time.

author: Josh Lurz <jlurz24@gmail.com>
commit message:
I've just committed the version of the code I have been working on for some time.

The major changes are:

-Code to create cost curves by running the model several times. The main portion of this code is in MACGeneratorScenarioRunner. This class wraps around Scenario and runs it multiple times. There is also a large amount of code in new Curve classes. These utility classes allow points to be associated with a Curve, and operations such as integration and interpolation to be performed on them. I will write up a document on this topic and send it out. I also need to spend more time verifying the results are comparable to miniCAM's.

Minor Changes:
-New code which reads in XML that allows you to delete an object in a scenario add-on. For instance, if I wanted to delete the Transportation sector I would read in

<scenario>
...
       <sector name="transportation" delete="1"/>
....
</scenario>

This will delete the object correctly. This has been added to the transportation scenario add-on so that the transportation scenario can be ran with the standard input. This is tested to work correctly.

-A new GDP object at the regional level. This work is not fully complete, however it has allowed GDP information to be removed from the Population object. Eventually all GDP functions will be moved into this class. This required minor structural changes to the base_input.xml file, so make sure you are running the updated version of this file.

-Changes to XML helper and toXML functions. The Tabs class which was formerly a static class is now properly passed as an argument. I have made all the appropriate updates, look at any toXML function to see how this is done. This is a correction of a design mistake I previously made. It is a minimal change conceptually, but does affect many lines of code. (If you'd like to know more about the C++ behind this, come talk to me or send me an email.)

-New functions in xml_helper.h which write out the beginning and end xml tag.

-main.cpp was reorganized so that multiple scenarios could be run correcltly. Most functionality was moved out of it.

-toDebugXMLOpen was moved in the initial period so that supplies and demands would be calculated by the time the debugging information was written. This makes the output consistent with other periods and much less confusing.

-fixed bug where base year supplies for fixed output technologies were not correct. (This was committed several days ago as it did change model execution)

-fixed bug in DemandSector price ratio in base period. This did not change the model execution, but did produce a bad output.

-Added two new directories to CVS, one for documentation and one for unit tests. These are seperate modules within the objects CVS source tree.

-Reduced number of Xerces dependencies which should hopefully reduce code compilation time.

-many small code cleanups made along the way.

You'll need to add the .cpp files in /util/curves/source and the new gdp.cpp in /containers so that it will link.

I've checked and the code I've committed causes less that .1% difference in all output values that I checked, which was quite a few. This is probably due to a slightly different solution path. If you notice any possible errors due to the changes I have made, please let me know as soon as possible. I also tagged CVS before I added any new code with the tag "pre_cost_curves", so that you may go back and get a version of any file without my changes. Let me know if you need help doing this.

-Lastly I compiled my code with the newest version of the Xerces libraries, so if you notice any incompatabilities try upgrading to this version at xml.apache.org.

author: Josh Lurz <jlurz24@gmail.com>
commit message: The new way reading in add-on files is very simple. There is an XML tag within configuration.xml called <ScenarioComponents>. Within this are elements, each of which is the name of an add-on file. They are read in in the order they are listed, although this should not matter with well written add-on files. The <Value> tag has a name attribute, but this is for convenience when viewing the file, it may be left blank. The RunningNonReference switch and the number of add on files have been removed. If the file is listed, the model will read it in.

commit message:
First I changed all of the SGM visits from update to start/end.  I also removed any checks on the period in the accept methods for SGM classes to the visitors.

I made expediture into an array so that we can have access to its values for all periods at the end of the model run when the XMLDB output happens.

I changed national accounts from and array of NationalAccount to and array of NationalAccount*. This allowed NationalAccount to reside in RegionSGM instead of Region.

I added and enumToXMLName to expenditure and NationalAccount so that the XML names of the enums are standardized.  I also changed the toDebug in those classes to take advanatage of the new method so each enum print is not hard coded.

I added SGM classes to XMLDBOutputter so that their values can be written to the database. 
I split Region into an abstact base Region and a RegionMiniCAM.  During this split National Accounts got moved into RegionCGE and well as updateMarketplace.

I also changed Input to store a vector of price paid and demand currency. This allows all output to occur at the end of the model run. This required changing several interfaces to include a period argument.

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message: Numerous changes for RCP.  In the PP added the ability to read data as the entire globe and not break it down into regions.  In the DM updated the create NetCDF routine to be more flexible in terms of including many variables, additonal info about each variable, and having the dates that go into the netcdf be relative to any year.  More flexible scalar variable so that it can read multiple vars from the same input xml file.  The CSV file manager will remove any files it was managing after they get written out.  Many updates to the emissions downscaler which include actually creating the PP variable as a result of the downscaling, the input vars are dm vars as apposed to pp vars, fixes with regards to edge case scenarios like when a region does not have data in the end years, or when we don't actually want the emissions to converge with in a region.  Also added some more debuging options into the downscaler.  Both the DM and PP can now be run via a bath script.

commit message: During a model run, GCAM spends a significant amount of its time in a few loops in a ASimpleCarbonCalculator. author: Robert Link <robert.link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Output solver diagnostic trace in canonical order.

The vector markets seen by the solver can change between invocations
as the solution-info-filter adds or drops markets from the solution
set.  This causes some markets to jump around in the output, making
it hard to identify markets that seem to be causing solution problems.
This development adds a canonical ordering to the markets in the
calculation.  Solvers that produce diagnostic data will use this
ordering to ensure that the numbering of markets stays consistent in
the output.

author: Robert Link <robert.link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Eliminate maximum line length in Logger class.

The Logger class used a fixed-length buffer to marshall data
for output, causing lines to be forced to wrap at 5000 characters.
This buffer has been replaced with a managed buffer that expands
as necessary to accommodate arbitrarily long lines (subject to
total memory available).

author: Robert Link <robert.link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Change solver-data-log output to "long" format.

Previously we used a "wide" format, which placed all of the output from
a single iteration on the same line.  This forced us to decide in advance
how many markets we wanted to have and to fill in any non-participating
markets with NaN values.  The long format obviates these problems, which allows
us to output price, supply, and demand for all markets, not just the ones
currently being solved.

This patch also includes some minor documentation fixes and changes to how
we calculate the defaults in the plotting functions.

author: Robert Link <robert.link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Ensure that the baseCost parameter is always set during calibration.

Previously, it was possible for a sector with several subsectors, all with
zero share weights in the base year, to get through the calibration subroutine
without setting a value for the baseCost parameter for the discrete choice
function.  In the absolute-cost-logit, this causes NaN values for shares in
these sectors.  Even though these sectors were not producing anything, some
of the NaN values escaped into output data.  Now, in such cases baseCost will
be set to 1, and a warning will be logged to the calibration_log.

This fixes the bug reported in issue JGCRI-90

Update all headers to new DEFINE_VARIABLE syntax.  Now we use type flags
to distinguish between SIMPLE, ARRAY, and CONTAINER data instead of
different Macros for each.  This provides more flexiblity to exapand
later (think STATE flags) and makes the writing of the Macro utils
simplier.

Inherit containers from INamed or IYeared as appropriate.  Now we do not
need to market data definitions as named or yeared and instead
GCAMFusion will attempt to detect this automatically by checking if a
type is derived from INamed or IYeared.

Remove INamed from IStandardComponent and instead make the
connection directly; Fix up GCAMFusion to use the new strategy for
tagging containers and make flags to get event notifications for
processData, pushFilterStep, and popFilterStep boolean template
arguments to GCAMFusion instead of type flags on the DataProcessor type.

Parser for CSV headers

Code in `utils.R`, plus test code, to parse any headers at the top of
CSV files we read in. Handles .csv, .zip, and .gz files. If any of the
supported fields (`Title`, `Units`, `Comments`, `Description`,
`Reference`, `References`) are found, their data are added as
attributes to the data object. Multi-line attributes are supported
(e.g., multi-line comments).

Addresses #78 and also fixes #83 .

author: Ben Bond-Lamberty <bondlamberty@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
New less-strict 'sum test' for oldnew

I couldn't get the L101.ag_HA_bm2_R_C_Y and L101.ag_Prod_Mt_R_C_Y
outputs to pass tests, even though I could confirm that they're holding
the same data. I'm pretty sure this is because the old data system
writes data out using write.csv while we're using readr::write_csv and
subtle differences creep in, probably more so as one progresses through
the data system.

The best thing I could think of was to create a less-strict test, that
compares the sums of all numeric columns (as opposed to using
all.equal). Your code now tags these two datasets (and only these two)
with a flag to use this test. Not perfect, but everything now passes,
and it should still give us a warning if things change.

author: Robert Link <robert.link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Improve screening for use of forbidden functions

The screening function is now an actual (internal) function in the
package, with tests of its own, which the chunk test code calls on
each module function.  In the process we corrected some broken regular
expressions and added some edge cases.  This should eliminate some
potential false positives in the screening.  Finally, we have upgraded
the info message when this test fails to show the lines that have
forbidden calls in them.

We have also added `merge` to the list of forbidden functions.
Unfortunately, this breaks a formerly working chunk, but at least we
got to test the new info message.

Ironically, the new screening function uses `rbind` and `cbind` (which
are both on the forbidden list) internally to build its output matrix.

author: Robert Link <robert.link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Increase the `guess_max` parameter in read_csv to 10M lines.

This is sort of a proxy for "the whole file".  It turns out that
read_csv won't let you specify an arbitrarily large value for this
parameter.  It tops out at some random-looking number north of 20M.  I
went with the 10M figure as a nice, round number that should be
sufficiently large.

This changes fixes a couple of bugs related to read_csv mistakenly
detecting a column as integer if all of the entries up to `guess_max`
look like integers.  Then, if it sees a floating-point number
somewhere down the line, it chokes.  Scanning far enough that you can
be sure of seeing the floating point values is the simplest
workaround.

Addressed Sonny's comments by calculating average instead of reading it in, used OLD_DATA_SYSTEM_BEHAVIOR to use slightly different average values, and used left join error no match by reversing dataframes when joining. Please note my summarise_all line and if that's the most efficient way to compute the average.

Sonny's comments:
"I see a couple of problems with the data and above code. The original data has an average row, representing the average of the capacity factors, not including the 0 capacity factors. Calculating the average is what we should be using the DSR for, rather using a read in value. If someone changes the capacity factor for a state, the average would be wrong. I also noticed the average is slightly off. Please rewrite to do in code.
You should gather only once and then separate out the average from the state data. Then you can take the average of the state data, or use the read-in average for old code behavior. The left_join_error_no_match should be used. We want to ensure values for all state."

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Change the strategy for how GCAM fusion data definitions are done for
performance reasons.
Instead of holding all data containers memory in a fusion vector of Data
structs the member variable definitions are created as direct member
variables of the class and the vector of Data structs will instead hold
references to them.  In addition the vector of Data structs are only
instantiated upon request via a generateDataVector() method.
In this way the memory usage of the GCAM classes are the same as they
were prior to GCAM fusion thus no performance penalty.  The downside is
there is an added performance penalty when calling GCAM fusion however
since it shouldn't be called during World.calc this trade off is not so bad.
Also note that this alleviates some of the member variables restrictions
GCAM fusion used to impose: use initializer list for member variables
and we can use compiler generated copy constructors (as appropriate).

author: Ben Bond-Lamberty <bondlamberty@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Changes to timeshift test definition

The timeshift test isn't testing what we want, actually. What we care
about is the ability to adjust HISTORICAL_YEARS and FUTURE_YEARS,
basically, parameters that control what data GCAM treats as past versus
present. It doesn't (and shouldn't) need to change things like
AGLU_HISTORICAL_YEARS because this relates to how we process this
particular dataset. These two things are confounded across much of the
data system.

This commit (i) makes the timeshift change only HISTORICAL_YEARS and
FUTURE_YEARS and (ii) skip the timeshift entirely for LB125’s tolerance
check.

author: Robert Link <rplzzz@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Merge pull request #694 from JGCRI/xml-verify

Add a utility to compare output XML files to the corresponding files from the original data system. The comparison utility is written in python, but there is a test case that runs the comparison on each output file produced by the system as part of the overall test suite. Because the comparison data is too large to include in the repository, the system looks for the location of the comparison in an option called gcamdata.xml_cmpdir. If the option is not set, then the XML comparison test is skipped.

The comparison can also be run stand-alone from the command line. This is useful when you know a file is failing its comparison, and you want to capture the differences to diagnose the problem. There is also a shell script to run the comparison on all of the data system output files, for cases where you want to run all the comparisons, but not the rest of the package tests. The script takes the new data directory and the old data directory as arguments and loops over all the files it finds in the new data directory, finding the corresponding comparison file and running the comparison.

commit message:
Expand the range of price in unconventional oil supply curves.

The old curves had a massive amount of unconventional oil coming online
in a very small price range.  Apart from causing solution problems, this
also didn't seem very realistic.  We've left the bottom of the supply curve
the same as it was, but we've expanded the range by a factor of 5, which
should result in smoother introduction of unconventional oil into the
scenario and fewer solution problems.

author: Link, Robert P <Robert.Link@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Merge pull request #7 in JGCRI/gcam-core from feature/param-reset-api to master

Merge GCAM Fusion

Core model proposal CMP-249

* commit 'afad9a47a69a4f35a40d0c25ec7904ea0ffc22ce': (57 commits)
  Visual studio project fixes and minor warning corrections.
  Clean out no longer needed testing and example source files
  Cleanup commented out GCAM_PARALLEL code which changed after switching to centrally managed state strategy.
  Fixes for DEBUG_STATE which broke after cleanp.
  Better error checking and logging Reorder GCAMFusion template params so ProcessData is true by default and the last param since it is least likely to change.  Update calls to GCAMFusion accordingly.
  Add a bunch of comments to GCAMFusion and other such clean up.
  Clean up and better comment state related changes.
  Avoid storing sequestered emissions in GHG and instead just in the sequestration device.  NOTE: the logic in the sequestration devivce was flawed leading to sequestration of gases other than the target gas (in practice this means sequestering Non-CO2 gases).  This is fixed but means that results will be slightly different in policy runs.
  Some cleanup from things that broke during "state" changes with the exception of sequestered emissions which actually looks like it is broken (only noticable in the output DB however).  That fix will come in it's own commit.
  Given the new strategy for hold fusion data's lifting of restrictions for inline initilizer list revert atleast some of the vector initializations to be done inline instead of in the body of the constructor.
  Change the strategy for how GCAM fusion data definitions are done for performance reasons. Instead of holding all data containers memory in a fusion vector of Data structs the member variable definitions are created as direct member variables of the class and the vector of Data structs will instead hold references to them.  In addition the vector of Data structs are only instantiated upon request via a generateDataVector() method. In this way the memory usage of the GCAM classes are the same as they were prior to GCAM fusion thus no performance penalty.  The downside is there is an added performance penalty when calling GCAM fusion however since it shouldn't be called during World.calc this trade off is not so bad. Also note that this alleviates some of the member variables restrictions GCAM fusion used to impose: use initializer list for member variables and we can use compiler generated copy constructors (as appropriate).
  Simplify collecting/reset state to speed up the process. Avoid copying Value classes, espcially when they are state.
  Stash upper/lower supply curve bounds in solution info since retrieving them from iinfo requires synchronization and so slows down parallel jacobian calculations.
  Add back in parallel nullSupplyDemand, clean up no longer used expiremental parallel optimization flags from linux build.
  Fix LUC emissions to properly handle state which I had skipped previously.  Note this could amount to significantly more state to track and slower model performance and more memory useage.  I tried to mitigate this as much as possible by avoiding storing results when run during World.calc.  This fixes some crashes when running in parallel especially when running with lots of processors.
  Changes to allow computation of partial derivatives in parallel.
  Clean up prior handling of "state" variables by using the new centrally managed state Values instead.
  Attempts at speeding up state lookup
  First cut to manage "state" in a central location.
  Convert HectorModel to use DEFINE_DATA as it got left out when the rest of IClimateModel got converted since it wasn't being compiled by default.

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Changes logits after 02-14-2018 meeting in which we discussed how to
clean up the code for consistency in both the energy and ag uses.

In particular we avoid using the term "cost" and instead use "value"
since in the energy system the logit functions will operate on costs and
in the ag it will be profit rates.

No longer choose node profit rates to be the implied/intrinsic value and
instead just use the profit rate of the dominant child in the nest.
This simplifies the code and makes it so that we no longer have to cary
and "output value" and "base value".  We also no longer need to even
calculate the implied/intrinsic value any more.

Add in some error checking to ensure logits have the correct sign
depending on where it is used.  Also ensure that "base value" is never
negative as this would result in sharing working in the wrong direction
(increased profit rate leads to lower share for instance).

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
When I was cleaning up land_allocator code I mistakenly thought that all
land nodes / leaves needed to be able to store land allocation as model
computations occurred.  I was mistaken, we only need to store it:
* At the root (LandAllocator) and it's value does not change during
model operation (not STATE)
* At the leaves where they do change during model operation (STATE)

This only meant we were allocating some memory we were never using.
I've updated the member variable definitions accordingly anyways.

Merge pull request #61 in JGCRI/gcam-core from integration/water-ssp-merge-4.4 to master

Adding water demand, new land regions, new land technologies, and SSPs!

* commit '0bd641112bebf94ba769a07539c5a059393be7de': (183 commits)
  Update version number to 5.0
  Remove duplicate policy / config files which are no longer needed.
  Address PR comments: update comment to explain discount rate.
  Address PR comments: update name of coefficient
  Fix up queries for integration branch / catch up to 4.4
  Update Visual Studio project file to include readin_control
  Address more PR comments
  Address most PR comments
  When I was cleaning up land_allocator code I mistakenly thought that all land nodes / leaves needed to be able to store land allocation as model computations occurred.  I was mistaken, we only need to store it: * At the root (LandAllocator) and it's value does not change during model operation (not STATE) * At the leaves where they do change during model operation (STATE)
  Changes logits after 02-14-2018 meeting in which we discussed how to clean up the code for consistency in both the energy and ag uses.
  Avoid setting share-weight for future years in the land allocator during World.calc as this fails DEBUG_STATE.  Instead we will just calculate them in postCalc of the final calibration year.
  More cleanup with merge following testing SSPs and SPAs: * Update batch files to include feedstocks + neg emiss budget * Avoid crashes in dep finder when we have linked CO2 market and neg emiss policy * Generate SPA specific neg emiss policies which for now is just always regional but in the future could define different levels of budget.
  Additional fixes post gcam-v4.4 merge to get the model running again.
  modifications to ag cost methods that merge core model update to price/cost years (performed in Jan 2017) with integration branch modifications (latter modifications mostly pertained to the change from AEZs to water basins)
  Updating mapping file to correctly capitalize UrbanLand
  Updating land data system files to fix a basin mapping issue
  Fix up SSP+SPA batch files to consistently use IRR_MGMT.
  Print the name of the configuration file into the main log.
  Move configuration_water_mgmt.xml to configuration_ref.xml

author: Kyle, G Page <pkyle@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
revisions to municipal and industrial water demand calculation to address several issues
* municipal water interpolation/extrapolation took place after aggregating countries to regions
* municipal and industrial water demands had macro-region-level characteristics assigned directly to GCAM regions (should go to countries first, then get aggregated)
* industrial water demand was estimated from a purely bottom up method; this revision applies a top-down check to prevent unrealistically high withdrawal volumes
* industrial water demand was estimated from processed, region-level industrial TFE. this commit switches the estimator to country-level industrial electricity.

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
OLDNEW for LA114.wind; which switches to a different strategy for
evaluating the country level wind supply curves (we wanted to do so for
a couple of reasons: avoid excessive loops, and vastly speed up the
calculation).  The OLD_DATA_SYSTEM just read the previous price points
from temp-data-inject because the old method was so slow.

The old approach was to continue to evaluate the curves until the value
wasn't changing anymore with in some tolerance (with some minumum number
of calculations to ensure we don't quit in a shallow start to the
curve).  The new approach would only evaluate prices evenly spaces from
min.price to the 95th percentile of max production (the percent is
configurable)

Note this removed the need for
temp-data-inject/L114.OLDregional_price_supply_points.csv the last
temp-data!

commit message:
* revision to method for reconciling FAO and Monfreda/LDS, so that crops are aggregated to GCAM commodities first.
This reduces the "foddergrass" losses (50% of global total) that would otherwise happen from unmatched crops in the 2 databases.
* revision to the methods for computing fertilizer consumption by country and crop, to avoid the possibility for fodder crop
discrepancies to lead to very high IO coefs. Builds on prior work on this topic a few years ago.

- a slight modification to constants.R
- modifications to 4 chunks, plus updated documentation for 1 chunk (zchunk_L244.building_USA.R) which produces new outputs

commit message:
Merge pull request #75 in JGCRI/gcam-core from feature/reduce-luc-memory to master

* commit '5978155282491a56ae5f282e27c203e1485e849e':
  Add more comments to ICarbonCalc::CarbonCalcMode to give more details on when it is appropriate to run in each mode and what the purpose of doing so would be.
  Need to save previous timestep land allocation and carbon stock as those may have been re-calculated with a different future already.
  We need to make sure we don't reset the carbon stock we running the carbon calc in "reverse".
  Use boost::flyweight to share precalc_sigmoid between carbon calcs that have the same mature age.
  Drop to capability to set above/below ground carbon densities by year. It isn't a feature that we are taking advantage of and can easily add it back in later if we need it.
  Avoid storing LUC emissions by period just for the ability to back them out if we need to re-run that period again, such as for target finding. Instead add the ability to run the carbon calc in "reverse", i.e. re-calculate the LUC emissions just to back them out of the stored totals.

author: Kyle, G Page <pkyle@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
regional ag markets: input data files from FAO, assumptions tables, constants, R code, package data, and documentation.
* revisions to existing FAO data generally involve extending the data to the year 2012 and dealing with changes in country and commodity names
* R code changes compute regional prices, replace default global prices with regional prices, update the fertilizer prices (for accuracy,
* consistency with model output), revise the method of ensuring positive land profit rates (subsidy instead of revision to water coefs),
* reduce fertilizer demands in several nations with extremely high coefs (Morocco, Pakistan "other" crops), compute gross trade volumes
* from FAO bi-lateral trade data, and add in all necessary sectors and technologies for tracking gross trade by GCAM region in a new
* xml file.
this is done as a single commit because a partial version of these changes wouldn't build and run.

commit message:
This commit includes:
- Updates to zchunk_LB1235.elec_load_segments_USA.R and zchunk_L2242.elec_hydro_USA.R based on feedback from Pull Request #83: 271 Consolidated GCAM-USA updates
	- NOTE:  for zchunk_LB1235.elec_load_segments_USA.R, several outputs which are not used anywhere in gcamdata were removed
- Removal of gcamusa.USE_REGIONAL_ELEC_MARKETS from constants.R, and all places in gcamdata where it was used.  This is no longer a user configuration option we wish to maintain.
- Modification of the way gcamusa.USE_REGIONAL_FUEL_MARKETS (constants.R) is utilized.  We now always create regional fuel markets (at the grid region level) which pull from the national equivalent, and use this variable only to determine whether or not a regional cost “adder” is created (to match historical regional prices from EIA). There are a number of corresponding changes to various chunks where gcamusa.USE_REGIONAL_FUEL_MARKETS was previously used to indicate whether regional or national fuel markets should be created.  This simplifies the maintenance of this user configuration option substantially.
- Renaming several modules to use "module_gcamusa" rather tham "module_gcam.usa", plus associated documentation updates.

commit message:
calibration of multiple feedstocks for base-year biofuel production. includes:
* fractional secondary outputs in base years (using exogenous prices; default prices based on EU-15, the region with the greatest diversity of biofuel feedstocks)
* set_subsector_shareweights revised to allow user-specified value columns (was hard-wired to calOutputValue; change includes updates to documentation and tests)
* calibrated values based on IIASA/GLOBIOM data on biofuel consumption by feedstock, source (domestic production vs inputs) and region
* this revision has a large increase in DDGS and feedcakes prices from 2010 to 2015

author: Patel, Pralit L <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Merge pull request #97 in JGCRI/gcam-core from plp/feature/resource-reserve to master

* commit '83669dcea36aea2edcb9849db052b83bcbf16e94': (31 commits)
  Move reserve calculation out of level 1 into level 2 as they rely on model base years
  Remove Dep from R object names to be consistent.  Update package data and documentation after that.  Verified the XMLs do not change as a result.
  Address most PR comments.  At this point I am going to rename a bunch of R obejects and which point I will take care of the rest of the comments
  Phase out resource calibration "price-adder" by 2100 for all fossil resource types
  Adjust depleteable resource tech change assumptions so that the overall resource results do not depart so strongly, namely more coal and less gas, from the current Core model.
  Extend resource reserve lifetimes to ensure available resources can never be stranded per proposal review comments.
  Update GCAM-USA resource inputs to include a technology shell in the resource.
  Move adding meta data for L111.RsrcCurves_EJ_R_Ffos inside of prebuilt data check since otherwise we may attempt to double add it when we do not have proprietary data.
  Update non-co2 resource queries in such a way to make them backwards compatible with the old model as well.
  Sum up annual production in reserve-subresource so that it can get set at the resource level.  This allows us to avoid changing the query for resource production thus maintain backwards compatibility in the query.
  Update package documentation
  Rebuild package data
  Include sources for assumed fossil resource production lifetimes
  Update Visual Studio project file for RR source code changes
  Bump down unconventional oil production lifetime to be more inline with literature.
  Fix missing resource technology for EGS which gets added in advanced geothermal scenarios only.
  Add some more comments to reserve data processing code and re-organize to make sure we have proper behavior with/without pre-built data.
  Get rid of environCost and serveranceTax as we will just use the technology to tack on extra costs now
  Move environCost to just a cost adder to the tech
  Data system changes to reflect buildup / decline phase being explict paramaters in the data system and spliting RR tech lifetime / average production year
  ...

commit message:
First cut at solver improvements including:
* Updating price/quantity scales using hueristics
* Constrain bisection that it can not make the entire solution worse
than one order of magnitude in a bracket step and keep walking back that
step by half until it does.
* Update the "supply correction" slope to match the self deriv according
to hueristics
* Multiply the land constraint policy price by 1e6 so that market prices
can be in the range of 1 but the adjusted value will be in the right
range for profit rates

curves.  Finally we fix the bug which was dropping tech change for
resources.

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
A number of solver tweaks and minor bugfixes including:
* Revert to initial condition if after bracketing the overall solution
became more than three orders of magnitude worse.
* Cap SmoothRenewableResource at production of getSmallNumber to avoid
the extremely flat section those curves produce, and instead rely on the
solution floor to clear these
* A number of preconditioner hueristics and be more careful with regards
to setting price/demand scalers particularly with regard to small values
* Ensure FoodDemand trial shares are capped to be between zero and one
* Ensure FractionalSecondaryOutput does not extraploate below the supply
curve (and get negative coefficients)
* Make Technology::mMarginalRevenue a STATE variables instead of just
mutable, even though it could only make a difference when running in
parallel and bad luck.
* Make TrialValue markets explictly respect supply curve bounds
* Clear the calculated lower supply curve bound so subsequent target
finder dispatches are re-calculate it with the correct amount of
depletion

commit message:
Pull request #200: Solver Updates and Library Changes

Merge in JGCRI/gcam-core from plp/feature/svd-parallel-default to master

* commit '9bcad98535760014ba0afaef0bea8cb5dcbd5cb5':
  I must have added the "wrong" ModelInterface.jar (the one for rgcam). This is the right one.
  Pull in testing framework updates for new libs
  Remove extra build configurations which are no longer needed in the Xcode project file
  Changes to update to BaseX-9.5.0
  Remove old LAPACK and TBB build targets from Visual Studio project file. Also remove 32 bit config as it will never work these days.
  Update Makefile configure files to update paths for PIC, ensure MKL still works with Eigen, and clean out all the LAPACK stuff
  Add max-parallelism int to configuration files
  Update visual studio project file
  Small fix to ensure compatibility with newer versions of TBB
  Add a new param to broyden to limit the maximum number of time you can re-use the Jacobian matrix in a broyden step.  If set to zero it collapses to a regular NR algorithm and therefore we can drop lognrbt as duplicative and don't have to maintain both.
  A bunch of solver related cleanup
  Clean up with respect to TBB and making sure we can easily turn it on/off still
  A number of solver tweaks and minor bugfixes including: * Revert to initial condition if after bracketing the overall solution became more than three orders of magnitude worse. * Cap SmoothRenewableResource at production of getSmallNumber to avoid the extremely flat section those curves produce, and instead rely on the solution floor to clear these * A number of preconditioner hueristics and be more careful with regards to setting price/demand scalers particularly with regard to small values * Ensure FoodDemand trial shares are capped to be between zero and one * Ensure FractionalSecondaryOutput does not extraploate below the supply curve (and get negative coefficients) * Make Technology::mMarginalRevenue a STATE variables instead of just mutable, even though it could only make a difference when running in parallel and bad luck. * Make TrialValue markets explictly respect supply curve bounds * Clear the calculated lower supply curve bound so subsequent target finder dispatches are re-calculate it with the correct amount of depletion
  Add back in SVD with a 0 threshold and fix bug with failed line search
  Make various solver tweaks made in other branches such as ATB or Macro. Also do some more experimentation about how/when/which matrix decomposition solver to use.  At the moment relying more heavily on FullPivLU
  Use right size for Eigen matrices
  First cut at being able to configure the maximum number of threads to use
  First cut at making parallel default but taking out start up overhead
  First cut at swapping in Eigen along with some other solver tweaks.
  Clean up, re-organize UBLAS vector/matrix definitions to easily swap to something else accross all solver related methods.

author: Alan V Di Vittorio <avdivittorio@lbl.gov>
commit message:
Update to GCAM6 with functioning land feedback

This includes gcam spinup functionality to generate baseline and restart gcam files
(which have been generated and stored in the inputdata directory).
The gcam namelist has been updated and new defaults set that point
to the inputdata directory.
PFT to gcam land type has been updated.
land scalar calculation has been updated to deal with some bad input
data (this may need to be re-updated later when the inputs are updated).
Emissions downscaling has been updated to read in baseline data.
Some additional arguments were added to get namelist values.
GCAM runs annually with annual land scalar updates.
New xml inputs are used for GCAM6, but they have been updated to exclude
fuel wood harvest.
Reading and writing of scalars and baselines have been updated for CSV files
(this includes the baseline elm files for scalar creation).
The eigen library header has been included here and is pointed to by the e3sm
build scripts.
Also set a compiler option in E3SM to not run GCAM in paralled because the
libraries are not present.
Some additional diagnostics are output.

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Some solver tweaks including:
* Ensure we fix any forcasted price for the negative emissions budget >
  1 as that will make the market singular and cause subsequent issues.
* Fix logic that prefers setting an initial price to last period rather
  than use an "unreliable" forcasts
* Cap "large/small" derivatives which are usually just a result of
  discontinous behavior.  This lets us apply a reasonable threshold
during SVD as well.

author: Pralit Patel <pralit.patel@pnnl.gov>
commit message:
Prior attempts to avoid prices > 1 for the negative emissions budget
have provent to be insufficient.  While prior attempts deal with it in
preconditioning, there is nothing to stop a solver component for running
into and derailing the solver inbetween precondition checks.

A better approach is to remove any caps in GCAM/CTaxInput.  Doing so
will create negative demands which does not make sense. However given
the supply will always be positive it could not solve to such a value.
And more importantly, we will always have continuous behavior even at "invalid" prices

commit message:
Updated GCAM restart control to behave like E3SM

The runGCAM function now takes an E3SM restart state argument and
controls setDensity (which is no longer called separately). The call
order is changed such that if the run is a restart run (or branch)
GCAM needs to run to set up its current state, then the scalars
are updated, then the current period is run. If it is not a restart
run the scalars are just updated before GCAM is run.

author: Alan V Di Vittorio <avdivittorio@lbl.gov>
commit message:
Completed CO2 downscaling

CO2 linearly downscaled grid values have been verified up to the point just prior
to being copied to the monthly arrays passed back to the fortran ehc. Restarts
also work properly. All base co2 data are now read in upon init, and the 2014
base grids are sclaed to 2015 base gcam global data. Annual scaling uses this
2015 grid as the reference (gcam scalars are also referenced to 2015). Aircraft,
international shipping, and other surface are downscaled separately. Base gridded data
have been updated accordingly, and a shell script has been added to gcam/tools
that generates the corresponding csv files (and their netcdf precurserors).The
convergence downscaling code has not been tested. GCAM still throws nan
floating point exceptions that the fortran code does not like. The boost
library has been added to the repo for portability.

commit message:
Updated scalar write to max precision

This isn't absolutely necessary, but it should enable
BFB duplication of a full-feedback run using the read scalar
capability with scalars written from a full-feedback run.
This isn't necessary because 6 decimals is more than enough
significant digits for these values; more than this is just a
numerical fact rather than value-added information.

Bug in TreeVector implementation. In some situation (Treevectors with almost same structure but just one extra TV layer) computations were performed twice, yielding erronimous results or only double work. Problem has been fixed and unit tests have been added (which should trigger the bug in older versions of OpenDA).

Affected methods:

The bug was present in various methods like 
*pointwiseMultiply
*pointwiseDivide
*dotProduct (more work but correct results)
*axpy

Note: bug was only triggered in localization related stuff combined with black box models as far as I could figure out.

ODA-405
An Internal compiler error (intel fortran 14 linux) is caused The combination of the (automake) macro F77_FUNC in combination with a fortran ISO binding f90 routine seems to trigger this issue.  Since I want to get rid of the F77_FUNC stuff (creating routines that match you fortran compiler) and replace it with proper ISO binding stuff (allows you to use an pre-compiled OpenDA version), I do not spent too much time in this issue
 Solution
 -> Remove the F77_FUNC macro and set default to what almost always works (lowercase_)
 ->Using a configure flag you can change it into uppercase.
 ->If you have a very creative fortran compiler just change the macro include/cta_system.h

commit message:
Replace deprecated `PAUSE` call with `READ`

A print is inserted before invoking `READ(*,*)` to notify the user of
the suspended state of the application. This is similar to the message
emitted by `PAUSE`. The behaviour is now slightly different:

- To continue: ENTER should be provided in stead of 'go';
- To terminate: a signal needs to be sent manually.

commit message:
Replace non-standard function SECNDS by SECOND

The non-standard function SECNDS is replaced by SECOND throughout the
source code. Since the alternative SECOND does not allow to provide a
reference time, the time difference is obtained by subtracting the
original reference value instead.

For details on the non-standard call:
https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.9.4/gfortran/SECNDS.html

moving the READ statement into a `DO WHILE` statement that runs until a
satisfactory read is performed.

This does not change the functionality, it merely makes the loop
explicit and thereby suppresses the compiler warnings.

author: Cees Voesenek <cees.voesenek@vortech.nl>
commit message:
Use Unicode paths for loading DLLs on Windows

Without the UNICODE define, the Windows API will use ANSI strings
instead of Unicode strings. The implementation in Costa assumes that
Unicode strings are used, and defines the library name as a 16-bit
WCHAR. Copying over a 8-bit char string to a 16-bit WCHAR string
effectively result in a \0 after that first character, hence e.g.
LoadLibrary will attempt to load a DLL with a name consisting of only
the first character of the string...

** major TOPPAS change

** most important changes:

 - suffixes of files in the pipeline are renamed by their content after Tool finished. Thus making the output much more accessible
 - Merge nodes fixed, i.e. file passing in general is much more robust now
 - a very potent "dry_run" is done before any tool is actually run, to uncover if input list length's etc could lead to a crash downstream
 - fixed some minor issues (see tickets above)

commit message:
[FIX] wrong parameter escaping introduced in [10522]
switching from system() to QProcess for fix.
here's the doc of system() for Windows (case 2 suddenly applied due to the former commit):
system() runs command as cmd /C command. And here's citation from cmd doc:
If /C or /K is specified, then the remainder of the command line after
the switch is processed as a command line, where the following logic is
used to process quote (") characters:

    1.  If all of the following conditions are met, then quote characters
        on the command line are preserved:

        - no /S switch
        - exactly two quote characters
        - no special characters between the two quote characters,
          where special is one of: &<>()@^|
        - there are one or more whitespace characters between the
          two quote characters
        - the string between the two quote characters is the name
          of an executable file.

    2.  Otherwise, old behavior is to see if the first character is
        a quote character and if so, strip the leading character and
        remove the last quote character on the command line, preserving
        any text after the last quote character.


So the fix would have been to add extra quotes around the whole command, but only for Windows. That seemed too much fragmentation.

[IO, DOC, FEATURE] * DecoyDatabase can now handle an arbitrary number of input files (not just a single FASTA file plus contaminant). This makes it easier to create target-decoy databases from multiple fasta files (e.g. if the sample contains multiple species, e.g. CElegans, EColi plus contaminants).

  individual spectra and chromatogram without loading them into memory

  offsets

  <chromatogram> tags

commit message:
[FIX, INTERNAL]

on Windows the tests below might fail when OpenMS is configured with a
OPENMS_GET_TEST_DATA_PATH which contains a small device letter, e.g.

//#define OPENMS_GET_TEST_DATA_PATH(filename) (std::string("c:/dev/oms/source/TEST/data/") + filename).c_str()

since getLoadedFilePath() used to call Qt to create absolute paths and
this changes "c" to "C", making the string comparison like

TEST_EQUAL(di2.getLoadedFilePath(), OPENMS_GET_TEST_DATA_PATH("File_test_empty.txt"))

fail. The fix here is to modify/fix the path only if its not absolute,
thus for our tests it will stay untouched since OPENMS_GET_TEST_DATA_PATH
is always absolute.

Alternatively, one could modify each(!) test (e.g. convert to lower case
before comparing),
but this creates invalid paths on unix and is error prone (since the next
developer will surely forget to use it).

Failing tests are

123 - ConsensusXMLFile_test (Failed)
126 - DTA2DFile_test (Failed)
130 - FeatureXMLFile_test (Failed)
142 - MS2File_test (Failed)
143 - MSPFile_test (Failed)
149 - MzDataFile_test (Failed)
153 - MzMLFile_test (Failed)
158 - MzXMLFile_test (Failed)

  warn about all files that include a header with static functions but

  matrixIsIdentityMatrix -> a warning will be emitted about the unused
  matrixIsIdentityMatrix function.

commit message:
[FEATURE,API] Support to wrap MetaInfoInterface in QVariant

These changes allow the MetaInfoInterface metadata class to be converted to
QVariant, and saved using the QVariant API. The changes in this class
would probably never directly be used, but instead in MetaInfoInterface
subclasses to simplify their changes to wrap in QVariant.

Specifically, the Q_DECLARE_METATYPE was used to wrap MetaInfoInterface and the
two required stream operators (using QDataStream) were added.

Note: the stream operators are a bit more kludgy than ideal for
MetaInfoInterface in order to handle DataValue types (i.e. converting
between QString/String to the appropriate DataValue), especially for
StringList, IntList, and DoubleList types.

commit message:
[FEATURE] Add new PeakInvestigator tool and library class

This commit has two parts:

1) Addition of a class to TRANSFORMATIONS/RAW2PEAK that calls the public
   API of PeakInvestigator (see information at veritomyx.com). This
   class handles calling the public API via web service calls, as well
   as the other necessary steps including reading a mzML file containing
   raw/continuum data, bundling these scans for upload to Veritomyx's cloud
   platform, transfers to/from the SFTP drop, extracting peak lists and
   writing to mzML.

2) TOPP tool (PeakInvsetigator) that makes extensive use of the
   associated library class.

The implementation of both parts is modeled after the PeakPickerHiRes and
PeakPickerWavelet tools and corresponding library classes.

commit message:
[FEATURE,API] Add PeakInvestigator as an external library

As suggested in pull request #1007, the PeakInvestigator class has been
moved into an external library as was done for OpenSwath and SuperHirn,
and split into several classes. Specifically, the following supporting
class have been created:

* TarFile for bundling/extracting scans from a MSExperiment to a gzip'd
  tarball.
* AbstractSecureFileTransfer that implements the core functionality for
  the (currently) two classes for SFTP transfers.
* LibSSH2SecureFileTransfer for SFTP transfers using libssh2.
* PSCPSecureFileTransfer for SFTP transfters using PuTTY's scp program.

This commit also adds the CMake files for bulding the library, but does
not touch the OpenMS files.

commit message:
[FIX] fixing segfault in MassTraceDetection

Fixes a major bug leading to a segfault and wrong output in
MassTraceDetection.

This error occured in MassTraceDetection::run when MS2 spectra are
present in the input_exp (which they are usually not since
FeatureFinderMetabo and MassTraceExtractor do not load them).

Rationale:
- MassTraceDetection works with a temporary MSExperiment work_exp which
  only contains part of the input data (not all spectra, not all peaks)
- The initial seed peaks are stored in chrom_apeces and need to be in
  the reference frame of the work_exp and *not* in the reference frame
  of the old input_exp
- Therefore, the pairs appended to chrom_apeces need to use
  (spectra_count, spec_peak_idx) and not (scan_idx, peak_idx)

Solution:
- use (spectra_count, spec_peak_idx) for chrom_apeces which maps
  correctly to work_exp

Fixes #1633

commit message:
[FEATURE] making algorithm order-independent

- The algorithm is now independent of the order in which QTCluster::add
  is called as the annotations are not computed on the fly after each
  addition any more but rather at the end. The criteria whether an
  elements get added to the cluster is whether it conflicts with the
  center point of the cluster and *not* whether it conflicts with the
  *current* best annotation set.
- This should make the algorithm independent of addition order when
  using ids and yield better performance

declaration of new sub-methods

modified:   ../src/openms/source/ANALYSIS/ID/AScore.cpp
* AScore::compute: split the method in sub-methods to achieve a better overview and
    to be able to test each sub-method separately.

* copy old hit and overwrite the values: otherwise the other meta values are lost (phospho = hit;)

* set score default to zero: if a peptide has no phospho-site event or the number of phospho-sites
  are equal to the number of phospho-events Ascore won't be calculated. If in that case the score is zero,
  instead of the old score value, there is no misunderstanding in the interpretation of the score values.
  The score value, set in the peptide hit after the Ascore calculation, is the weighted average score of the best peptide sequence out
  of all the possible sequence permutations based on the number of phospho-sites and phospho-events.

  --> Suggestion: also calculating the weighted average score for peptides, which have no phospho-site, phospho-site-event,
      or the number of phospho-sites are equal to the number of phospho-site-events (for these Ascore is not calculated, and so the score would be 0)

* ranking: calculation of ranking before calling the method determineHighestScoringPermutations.
    The ranking calculation is executed just once instead of twice.

* iteration of the windows_top10: the index of the current window was used
  as iteration limit to calculate the numberOfMatchedIons instead of the
  calculated depth of the maximum score difference between the two best scoring
  sequence permutations.

* absolute value to get 0 scores instead of -0 scores: -10 * log10(1) = -0

* AScore::computeSiteDeterminingIons: instead of starting the spectrum at 0, the lowest m/z value is rounded down
  to the next hundred value. Because of that windows with no matches at the beginning are not possible any more.

commit message:
[FIX] allow user to turn off mass trace length check

The check for the length of the masstrace does not make sense if the
mass trace detection is followed by elution peak detection as in the
MassTraceExtractor where long mass traces are split up. Instead what
happens is that MTD is extremely slow since it finds the same masstraces
again and again but is prevented from adding them to the result and move
on.

This commit allows to set max_trace_length to -1 and skip the length
check.

commit message:
1. Ascore test data:
The Ascore results differ to the results of the Ascore tool provided on the website http://ascore.med.harvard.edu/ascore.html
But it seems that the online version has some issues calculating the Ascore using the cumulative binomial probability formula.
E.g. with the values 6, 5, 0.06 for the variables N, n, p the calculated Ascore using WolframAlpha is 53.5337, which does not
conform to the result 53.57, which is mentioned in the paper (see Fig. 3c).
In addition the site determining ions calculation seems not reliable, because in some test cases more site determining ions
were calculated than it could be possible.
Another reason for the differences of the results could be the fragment ion tolerance used to match the theoretical spectra
with the real spectra. The value used in the Ascore tool provided on the website is not mentioned.

2. Calculation of site determining ions:
m/z values were rounded to two decimal places for comparison if m/z values differ. The number of decimal places can be set as parameter in the
TOPP tool PhosphoScoring. Default value is 2.

    two site determining ions could be one peak using the fragment mass tolerance.

commit message:
[FIX] PhosphoScoring

- corrected calculation of number of matched peaks (iteration limit was set wrong)
- if the peptide score of the two best scoring peptides is the same, Ascore is set to 0 because no further calculation is necessary.
- changes calculation of site determining ions:
  if two ion masses of the two best scoring theoretical spectra are matching, but another ion mass would also be within the tolerance, this ion within the tolerance should not become a site determining ion. Therefore I included a check if the next ions are also within the tolerance.

  Because of this the number of site determining ions of the two best scoring peptides can differ. Therefore for each peptide their specific number of site determining ions is used to calculate the cumulative binomial probability.

  E.g.: 441.209, 441.217 are all counted as one peak and 441.217 can not be seen as site determining ion
  441.209        441.209
  521.183        441.217

- Test: Ascores changed because of different number of matching peaks
        Added test case for different number of site determining ions

* changed strategie to convert Luciphor output sequences: replacing the lower case letters of the sequence using the defined modifications in the search parameter could lead to the problem that more modifications could be defined for the same amino acid. Therefore we changed the strategie to use the database search engine sequence as template and remove all modifications. Next all modifications != the set target modifications for Luciphor are set based on the original sequence (also the C- and N-term modifications). The predicted modifications of luciphor are set in a next step based on the result of Luciphor. Lower case amino acids matching the defined target modifications are then replaced.

commit message:
[FIX-#1740] MzTabExporter: modification "Phospho (ST)" throws error

[FIX] Parse Mascot XML - Terminal Modifications:
1. Mascot adds fixed modifications, which cannot be set, additionally as variable modification.
Error example: Fixed mod: "Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q)"
<warning number="1">'Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q)' can only be used as a variable modification; setting it to variable</warning>

Additionally added to variable modifications:
<SearchParameters id="SP_0" db="PhosphoLibrary_TD" db_version="PhosphoLibrary_TD_Oct15.fasta" taxonomy="All entries" mass_type="monoisotopic" charges="" enzyme="trypsin" missed_cleavages="4" precursor_peak_tolerance="5" precursor_peak_tolerance_ppm="true" peak_mass_tolerance="0.02" peak_mass_tolerance_ppm="false" >
  <FixedModification name="Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q)" />
  <VariableModification name="Oxidation (M)" />
  <VariableModification name="Phospho (ST)" />
  <VariableModification name="Phospho (Y)" />
  <VariableModification name="Gln->pyro-Glu (N-term Q)" />
</SearchParameters>

In OpenMS the fixed modification needs to be removed from the list.

2. Fixed modifications: N-term/C-term modifications on a specific amino acid are ignored.
If a terminal modification is set in the search parameters as fixed and it is defined for a specific amino acid, the specifity is ignored and
the terminal modification is set on every sequence in the Mascot idXML output.
Reason: in the mascot XML parsing step, amino acid specifications are not considered, when the fixed modifications are added to the sequence.

Set in all peptides as N-term modification:

commit message:
[FEATURE,NOP] filter peptide hits based on protein digestion products

This feature filters peptide hits and it is used as part of the
TOPP IDFilter pipeline.

It reads an input FASTA file and it loads individual FASTAEntry
structures.

Then it matches the accessions of the peptide hit and checks if it is a
valid digestion product of the protein sequence.

If peptide hit do not have a matching accession they are not filtered.

IMPORTANT:This feature is not handling peptide hits with unknown
parameters like UNKNOWN_POSITION or N_TERMINAL_POSITION.
This may cause unexpected behavior.

  often it comes up empty (e.g. no fragment ion scans are found).

  window (this assumes the user clicked on something interesting in the
  data such as a feature).

commit message:
flag `id:sequences_whitelist_enforce_exact_matches`

Introduced new FileFilter flag `id:sequences_whitelist_enforce_exact_matches`
that changes behavior when using `id:sequences_whitelist`.
Our new flag forces sequences to match sequences from the
whitelist *exactly*, rather than contain a substring from the whitelist.
We introduce the flag as advanced parameter as it serves a specific,
advanced use case.

completed docs

`id:sequences_whitelist`).

author: Moritz Freidank <freidankm@gmail.com>
commit message:
adding tests

FileFilter_45 demonstrates that the default behavior has not changed:
specifying a whitelist without setting
`id:sequences_whitelist_enforce_exact_matches` performs substring based
matches.
FileFilter_46 shows the impact of setting
`id:sequences_whitelist_enforce_exact_matches` on the same input as
FileFilter_45 - only the full sequence ["STLIPPPSK(Label:13C(6)15N(2))"]
gets matched, the match based on substring [YSFS] is no longer found.

commit message:
[FIX, API, TEST] mass calculations for isotope distributions

CoarseIsotopePatternGenerator used to output atomic numbers (# protons + # neutrons) for the mass of each isotope.
Now it has a calc_mass_ flag that can be set during initialization or later that determines if expected masses or atomic numbers should be returned.
Expected masses are the monoisotopic mass of the molecule + (C13_C12_MASS_DIFFERENCE * isotope number)
Unit tests were updated
pyopenms bindings were updated

fixes #3589

Feature/nested parallelization (#3679)

* [FEATURE] use nested parallelization

Use nested parallelization in OpenSWATH - we have two loops and if we have a certain number of threads, we cannot really increase the number of threads on the outer loop in any useful manner. Instead, we will parallelize over the batches using a set of inner thread workers.

author: enetz <eugen.netz@gmail.com>
commit message:
[FIX] TOPPView IDs from theo spectra

Because of synchronization between peak labels and PeptideHits,
PeakAnnotations were generated after matching to Theoretical Spectra
and these were kept and used after the second time an ID was chosen.
This lead to a changes in the ID view depending on whether you look at an ID for the first time.
Now the labels are synchronized and the theoretical spectrum deleted immediately
and the PeakAnnotations stored in the PeptideHits used right away.
This leads to the sequence coverage being shown immediately and a more consistent representation of IDs.

commit message:
[FIX] OpenPepXL and XFDR: grouping of top ranked hits by light spectrum

for labeled linkers the top x hits for each spectrum pair were treated separately,
which resulted in many more hits than x, sometimes with duplicates, reported for some light spectra, from combinations with different heavy spectra. This caused several redundancies and instabilities, while not adding any value.
This change groups all of these hits by common light spectra, reranks them and reports the top x reranked hits to every light spectrum regardless of the heavy spectrum.
If a user wants to see hits from more spectrum combinations, he can just increase the number of reported hits for each light spectrum.

commit message:
[FEATURE] OPXLLF: reduced memory usage by moving the parallel loop

previously the parallelized loop was looping over the spectra.
The list of candidates and results had to be enumerated and computed for each spectrum
and this increased the memory usage proportional to the number of used threads.
Now the parallelized loop loops over the candidates and results for one spectrum.

This leaves some code that was parallelized previously out of the parallelization for now, but does not slow down the algorithm significantly, while reducing memory usage by a factor almost equal to the number of used threads when it runs on more than one thread.

commit message:
[FIX] OPXL: fixed handling of "target+decoy" classification

"target+decoy" peptides were treated as decoys for XLMS data. They are now treated as targets.
Also the reporting of the XLMS specific "xl_target_decoy" MetaValue is now more complete and consistent.
It is reported on both the alpha and beta peptide, but combines the target_decoy state of both peptides: if any of the two peptides was only matched to decoy proteins, the whole cross-link is treated as a decoy. Otherwise it is a target.
This makes e.g. filtering out decoys after FDR calculation more straightforward.

author: Matthias Bernt <m.bernt@ufz.de>
commit message:
PSMFeatureExtractor differentiate list and single file input

The tool has two input modes single file input and
multiple file input. For the later case `-multiple_search_engines`
needs to be added.

These two cases can not be distinguished automatically
for automatic tool building (Galaxy).

One possible solution is to use two inputs and require exactly one of
them. Seems to be the least painful change for Galaxy tool building.
Alternatively I could "manually" influence the tool building
process.

Also adds tests.

[FEATURE,TEST] Change TextExporter output to display accession details

If a peptide has multiple protein accessions, the text export now contains multiple rows of the same peptide that are identical except for the accession column. That column contains the corresponding protein name and the start and end position of the match. This change reveals whether a peptide matches multiple times in the same protein, and where. These changes are reflected in outputs of TextExporter tests 3,4 and 5.

Closes #4668

[fix] Param::hasSection checks whether key has a trailing colon and removes it if so

Depending on whether a section was created with Param::addSection("Section1:Section2") or Param::addSection("Section1:Section2:"), i.e. with or without trailing colon, Param::hasSection would not work properly.
If a section was added Param::addSection("Section1:Section2") and was checked with Param::hasSection("Section1:Section2:") false was returned. Now the trailing in hasSection will be cut off so that it'll always find the right section if it exists.

Doxygen calls TOPPViewBase while generating the docs without the TOPPViewBase::TOOL_SCAN::SKIP_SCAN set so that TVToolDiscovery is called and tries to generate params for all tools.
Because doxygen is called from somewhere else than "~/build/bin" File::getSiblingExecutable and File::getExecutablePath fail because they mistake the directory doxygen is in for the executable directory.
Therefore said flag for TOPPViewBase needs to be set to prevent that.

commit message:
Support for overlapping IM and m/z windows (for diaPASEF data) (#5911)

* Add support for PASEF scans

Previously when processing diaPASEF data with overlapping m/z SWATHs
with different IM this would have to split up into multiple .mzML files
and processed seperately.

These changes enable PASEF with overlapping schemes (e.g. py3) to be
processed as one file.

* add name to authors list

* Ensure proper SWATH window is selected

Similar to PRM, transitions can be found in multiple SWATH windows when
PASEF is performed because there are windows with the same m/z however
different IM. Ensure that extraction occurs in the best SWATH. Best
SWATH is determined by the SWATH in which the transitions's IM is the most
centered.

* Add check for m/z swath

fix bug in which transitions were being extracted in m/z windows that
they were not in.

* clean up empty spaces and unnecessary prints

* add test for PASEF swath window processing

create a test with 3 precursors, over two swath windows with same MZ and
different IM. Test that this can be properly distiguished into 2 SWATH
windows and that each precursor is extracted from the window in which
its IM is the most centered.

* [FIX] create script outputs file # actually used

fixed bug where previously sample file outputs OpenSwath_18 and now
outputs OpenSwath_23 which is the .mzML that this script creates.

* More descriptive debug message

report the IM information on the SWATH window in which the precursor
will be added to.

* If overlapping windows add -sonar/-pasef reminder

If windows are overlapping in m/z or IM it may be because the user
forgot to add the -sonar or -pasef flag so add this reminder.

previous the tests I added did not pass, now everything should pass

test was failing because added ion mobility information to SwathMap.h.
Now test passes if default IM at -1.

* add swath file consumer test with IM

commit message:
change switchKR behaviour with nontryptic peptide

Previously if peptide did not end in K or R switchKR would replace the
last AA with a random AA. Here, the behaviour is changed such that if K
or R is not present, we keep the terminal AA. This new behaviour means
that the same nontryptic peptide sequence will always generate the same
decoy peptide.

commit message:
OpenSwathDecoyGenerator remove duplicates (#6054)

* change switchKR behaviour with nontryptic peptide

Previously if peptide did not end in K or R switchKR would replace the
last AA with a random AA. Here, the behaviour is changed such that if K
or R is not present, we keep the terminal AA. This new behaviour means
that the same nontryptic peptide sequence will always generate the same
decoy peptide.

* Add documentation on switchKR method

Not sure how to add to documentation without changing the format of the
method. So had to change return type from void to peptide

* Change test ouput for new switchKR method

* [FEATURE] check generated decoys are not targets

Add a check to check that decoy sequences generated do not happen to be
target sequences (this will cause an error in OpenSwathWorkflow). Also
added appropriate tests.

Current method works, but is quite slow with larger libraries.

* Speedup searching for decoys in targets

instead of searching using vector, search using unordered map for decoy
sequences in targets which drastically speeds up runtime

* [FIX] protein reference

this allows file to be converted to .tsv without error

* Revert "change switchKR behaviour with nontryptic peptide"

This reverts commit 79a090fb73bfa26db2dfaa05138300accde802aa.

5321022074118851ca895d68525b29dbb862f2f3 partially)

back to default.

* fix tests

replace tests output to reflect the new changes (to swtichKR for
openswathdecoyGenerator) and for dropping decoy duplicates (MRMDecoy_test)

* [FEATURE] check that decoys are not duplicated

with switchKR feature can randomly get 2 peptide sequences that are not
tryptic and almost identical generate the same decoy
e.g. PEPTIDA --> DITPEPQ and PEPTIDE --> DITPEPQ (Q is randomly chosen
for the final AA twice)

- Add check to ensure that this decoy sequence is not added twice

	- since hard to test the random nature of switchKR, add 2
duplicate target peptides and ensure the decoy is only generated once

ensure that this peptide does get a decoy generated for it (because it
is a different sequence)

[TEST] commented out OpenPepXLS's spec.xml tests

These tests are unstable due to differences in number to string conversions between versions of boost.
This can not be avoided or whitelisted due to the nature of the format (Base64 encoded strings in multi-line blocks).
Currently we see this difference between the boost versions <= 1.71.0 and >=1.78.0. It seems the boost developers are still working on the relevant code and further changes in future versions are likely.

The spec.xml format is only necessary for compatibility with the xQuest Result Viewer, which is low priority right now.
The tests can be activated again, if and when our number to string conversion becomes less dependent on updated external libraries.

commit message:
[Feature] OMS file format read/write speedup, v2

Reimplementation of #6147 due to merge conflicts.

Merges the DataValue table into each _MetaInfo table. This reduces file size by getting rid of DataValue ID numbers and therefore also writing speed.

Added backwards compatibility. All related tests run through without changes locally.

The numbers changed slightly due to other optimizations since the previous PR, but there is still a significant improvement:
on one example ~130mb idXML file,
OMS file size improved from ~130mb to ~110mb, writing speed from ~6.3s to ~5.3s, so about 15% faster.

commit message:
feat: adds parameter import via JSON

This allows to specify a JSON file, instead of a ini/ctd file as an
input to `-ini`. This allows workflows (e.g. CWL) to produce parameter
files that can be consumed by OpenMS tools.

About the Json input files:
    These file are a dictionary of key to values (scalar). Only the special case
    of files will require a map.

A small example file for SeedListGenerator:
```
{
    "in": {
        "class": "File",
        "path": "topp/PepXMLFile_test.mzML"
    },
    "test": true,
    "out_prefix": "test_cwl_",
    "threads": 1
}
````

Some programs have nested parameter, in this case two different key
synatxes can be used. Either keys with `algorithm:threshold` as OpenMS
also uses internally or `algorithm__threshold`. The second version is
required for external tools that don't handle ':' very well or have
special meanings.
e.g.:
```
{
...
    "algorithm:threshold": 10,
    "algorithm__type": "xml",
...
}
```

commit message:
Feature - reading parameters via JSON file (#6879)

* fix-test: let us close that CTD stream before checking

* feat: adds parameter import via JSON

This allows to specify a JSON file, instead of a ini/ctd file as an
input to `-ini`. This allows workflows (e.g. CWL) to produce parameter
files that can be consumed by OpenMS tools.

About the Json input files:
    These file are a dictionary of key to values (scalar). Only the special case
    of files will require a map.

A small example file for SeedListGenerator:
```
{
    "in": {
        "class": "File",
        "path": "topp/PepXMLFile_test.mzML"
    },
    "test": true,
    "out_prefix": "test_cwl_",
    "threads": 1
}
````

Some programs have nested parameter, in this case two different key
synatxes can be used. Either keys with `algorithm:threshold` as OpenMS
also uses internally or `algorithm__threshold`. The second version is
required for external tools that don't handle ':' very well or have
special meanings.
e.g.:
```
{
...
    "algorithm:threshold": 10,
    "algorithm__type": "xml",
...
}
```

commit message:
Speedup Ion Mobility OpenSwath Processing (#6479)

* First attempt at modifying DIA scores

Try to forgo filtering by ion mobility by
just computing scores directly from the IM spectra.

At the same time try to avoid adding up spectra by computing scores
directly from a list of spectra

It is still quite buggy and does not produce expected results.

* [TEST] fix tests and bugs with window integration

* [TEST] fix DIAScoring and DIAPrescoring tests

* [TEST] fix tests with new function signatures

* [FIX] check boundaries of vector when integrating

before would get some wonky values because integrate spectrum would not
stop at boundaries of the vector.

* remove unnccessary files

accidentally added tmp files, delete them here

* [FIX] bug in swathMapMassCorrection

* remove debug print statement

* [INTERNAL] adapt speedup changes to IM scoring

Instead of filtering and adding the entire spectra just go about looking
for the regions of interest

* [FIX][TEST] OSW 17 test

added error checks to ensure that IM is present before scoring.

* [INTERNAL] removed unused functions

this includes filterByDrift(), _getAddedSpectra() and old
integrateWindow() functions

* [TEST] fix fetchSpectrumSwath() test

restructure fetchSpectrumSwath() tests for the new implementation

* [TEST] fix SONAR tests

Add back methods that previously took away as they will be used for
SONAR. SONAR is likely quite inefficient since using the old methods.
(Have to resample/add the entire spectrum not just select regions)

* remove unused variables

* remove files was suppose to ignore

* Force returned IM value to be -1

in integrateSpectrum() if drift time is not present set IM to -1

other minor changes to test scripts

tests new integrate window functions with/without ion mobility as well
as special cases (e.g. empty spectra, empty arrays, no windows provided
etc.)

Swath map map correction test because the window boundaries were so
large in one example that the IM boundary would be a value less than 0. To account for this change implementation of
DIAHelpers::adjustExtractionWindow to set the value to 0 if lower boundary
is a value less than 0.

this test has been replaced with test 23_b which tests the same concept
of adding up spectra

off MS1 mode. This invovles updating the test files.

NOTE: Unsure if this is the best way to deal with this exception.

mobility was undefined for MS1 in this test example.
