mobility if it is false allowing the usage of the original

commit message:
Fix mac runner brew issues

This fixes an issue where brew updates packages already present on the runner after we install packages. This was a problem because it could lead to brew trying to overwrite links to things like /usr/local/bin/2to3 with versions installed as a dependency of updates to preinstalled packages (the azure integration specifically requires python3.11 at the time of writing). When we install python with brew we can specify to clobber everything that might already be in /usr/local/.

restore ability to use glpk (has been broken since OpenMS 3.0 at least)

Using `#cmakedefine01` the variable will always have a 0/1 value, which fixes the problem.

OpenMS does not compile when using GLPK (instead of COINOR) (#7626)

* restore ability to use glpk (has been broken since OpenMS 3.0 at least)
Reason: `#define COINOR_SOLVER @CF_USECOINOR@` produces `#define COINOR_SOLVER 1` if coin is present but yields `#define COINOR_SOLVER ` if glpk is present. This will not compile code which is using `#if COINOR_SOLVER==1` !!
Using `#cmakedefine01` the variable will always have a 0/1 value, which fixes the problem.

commit message:
Resolve undefined behavior w.r.t. basic_string<unsigned_char>

`std::char_traits<unsigned char>` has been undefined behavior since at
least C++11 and was recently removed in LLVM/clang.  Therefore the
latest version of XCode no longer allows:

    std::basic_string<unsigned char>

This means that OpenMS will no longer compile on macOS after recently
released system updates are installed.

I "fixed" the issue by replacing `std::basic_string` with
`std::string` and a cast.  Since SQLite is returning a UTF-8 character
string, there's a chance that string comparisons will not work the way
we expect if wide characters are returned.

I still need to verify that the `OSWFile` test is actually checking
the section of code changed in this commit.

commit message:
Fix path normalization to use string(REPLACE) instead of file(TO_CMAKE_PATH)

The file(TO_CMAKE_PATH) command incorrectly treats ':' in Windows absolute paths
(e.g., D:/path) as a path separator, causing path corruption. Replace with
string(REPLACE) which simply converts backslashes to forward slashes without
any other interpretation.

Quote list variables in message() calls to preserve separators

the elements without separators in certain contexts. Adding quotes ensures the
list elements are displayed with proper semicolon separators.

commit message:
Fix macOS segfault by disconnecting ostream before streambuf destruction

The issue was that std::ostream destructor tries to access the streambuf
during cleanup, but the streambuf is being destroyed at the same time.
This causes platform-specific segfaults on macOS. Solution: explicitly
disconnect the ostream from the streambuf using rdbuf(nullptr) after
flushing and before the streambuf destructor runs.

Co-authored-by: jpfeuffer <8102638+jpfeuffer@users.noreply.github.com>

author: copilot-swe-agent[bot] <198982749+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Fix macOS crash by moving file opening out of member initializer list

The crash on macOS was caused by exceptions being thrown during member
initialization in the constructor's initializer list. When Bzip2Ofstream
or GzipOfstream constructors threw exceptions (from open()), the
Bzip2OStreambuf/GzipOStreambuf was never fully constructed, but the
base std::streambuf was already initialized, causing undefined behavior
on macOS.

Fixed by default-constructing the file members and calling open() in
the constructor body after all base classes are fully constructed.

Co-authored-by: jpfeuffer <8102638+jpfeuffer@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Peter J. Jones <peter@jonesbunch.com>
commit message:
cmake: Don't mangle cached environment variables

When using CMake/CTest to write out a `CMakeCache.txt` file,
environment variables injected into a string variable, which is then
written to a file via CMake, results in the value of those variables
being mangled.

For example, CMake list variables such as `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` have
their semicolon separators removed, resulting in an invalid list and
errors downstream about missing libraries.

I'm not sure it's wise to do this in the first place, but I kept this
cache initialization system and fixed the issue by moving it out into
a shell script.

- Fixes Cython compilation issues with pyOpenMS bindings

  updated array indexing to use static_cast<size_t>()
- Updated Precursor.pxd for Cython: cdef enum -> cdef enum class
- Updated all usages across codebase (format handlers, analysis modules,
  TOPP tools, GUI components, tests) to use qualified enum syntax
- Added compile-time assertions to ensure array sizes match enum count

commit message:
Switch pyOpenMS to modern CMake-based build with pyproject.toml

This change modernizes the pyOpenMS build system to fully leverage CMake
for C++ compilation, with setup.py only handling wheel packaging.

Changes:
- Add pyproject.toml with PEP 621 metadata for modern Python packaging
- Simplify setup.py to only handle versioning and packaging
  (CMake now handles all C++ compilation via Python_add_library)
- Clean up env.py.in to remove variables no longer needed
  (compilation-related vars removed, only version/path/config vars kept)

The build flow is now:
1. CMake configures and generates env.py from env.py.in
2. CMake compiles OpenMS and pyopenms C++ extensions
3. setup.py/pip packages the pre-built extensions into a wheel

This aligns with PR #7939's goal of cleaner pyOpenMS builds and follows
the modern approach used by projects like PyArrow.

author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit message:
fix: constrain RT parameter within data bounds in EmgFitter1D

This addresses issue #6239 where FeatureFinderMRM reported RT values
outside the valid data range. Instead of explicitly padding the data
with zero-intensity points (as proposed in PR #8412), this implements
a more efficient "virtual padding" approach:

- Add a boundary penalty residual to the Levenberg-Marquardt objective
- The penalty is proportional to the distance outside the data range,
  scaled by peak height to be comparable to data residuals
- Update the Jacobian to include derivatives for the penalty term
- Only adds 1 virtual residual instead of O(n) padding points

This prevents the optimizer from shifting the peak center outside the
observed data range while avoiding memory allocation for padding and
reducing the number of residual evaluations per iteration.

Add test cases that reproduce the RT-outside-range scenario by
creating truncated data where the peak is near the edge.

author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit message:
feat: add configurable RT bounds constraint in EmgFitter1D

Make the RT boundary constraint configurable via parameter for
backwards compatibility:

- Add "fit_bounds:enabled" parameter (default: true)
- When true: RT is constrained within data range (fixes #6239)
- When false: original unbounded behavior (for compatibility)

The functor constructor now accepts optional rt_min/rt_max parameters
that default to +/- infinity (no constraint) when not specified.

Updated tests to demonstrate:
- Without bounds: RT can exceed data range (documents the bug)
- With bounds (default): RT stays within range (confirms fix)
- Default behavior uses bounds
- Lower bound constraint works correctly

author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit message:
fix: add hard clamp to guarantee RT stays within bounds

The penalty term is a soft constraint that guides the optimizer but
doesn't absolutely guarantee the result stays within bounds. Add a
final clamping step after optimization to ensure the RT parameter
is always within the data range when fit_bounds:enabled is true.

This two-layer approach:
1. Penalty guides optimizer toward valid solutions (better convergence)
2. Clamp guarantees the constraint is respected (robustness)

author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit message:
refactor: simplify RT bounds - auto-enable when bounds passed

Remove the fit_bounds:enabled parameter. The boundary constraint is
now automatically enabled when bounds are passed to the functor:

- Functor constructor has default params of +/- infinity (no constraint)
- fit1d() always passes data range bounds (fix always active)
- External code using functor directly can choose to pass or not

This is simpler and more intuitive - the behavior is controlled by
whether bounds are provided, not by a separate parameter.

Add <algorithm> include and clamp the initial retention time guess

commit message:
Add platform-specific wheel support for pre-built extensions

The simplified setup.py was creating pure Python wheels (py3-none-any)
because setuptools didn't know about the CMake-compiled extensions.

Add BinaryDistribution and bdist_wheel_platform classes to:
- Tell setuptools the package has extension modules (has_ext_modules)

This ensures wheels are correctly tagged with platform info (e.g.,
cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_34_x86_64) instead of py3-none-any, preventing
filename collisions when merging wheels from different platforms.

discarded because they appeared to belong to multiple distinct protein groups.

commit message:
Add pre-find for OpenMS dependencies in standalone builds

When building pyOpenMS standalone (not as part of the OpenMS tree),
find_package(OpenMS) calls find_dependency() for all OpenMS dependencies
(Eigen3, Qt6, LIBSVM, etc.). These can fail if the dependencies aren't
findable in the current environment.

This commit:
- Pre-finds OpenMS dependencies before calling find_package(OpenMS)
- Caches found dependency locations to help find_dependency() succeed
- Adds a clear error message explaining how to fix standalone build failures
- Documents the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH requirements in pyproject.toml

Note: Standalone builds against a build directory (vs installed OpenMS)
may still fail because OpenMSConfig.cmake modifies CMAKE_MODULE_PATH to
include its own FindXxx.cmake modules, which may have different behavior.
For reliable standalone builds, use an installed OpenMS:

  cmake --install OpenMS-build --prefix /opt/openms
  export OpenMS_ROOT=/opt/openms
  pip wheel .

commit message:
Fix MSSpectrum.get_df() implementation for pyOpenMS

This commit fixes the implementation of get_df() and get_data_dict() methods
for MSSpectrum, addressing issue #7966.

Key changes:

1. MSSpectrum.pxd: Removed incorrect C++ method declarations (DataFrame get_df()
   and void get_data_dict()) - these methods are implemented in Python/Cython,
   not in C++.

2. MSSpectrum.pyx addon:
   - Removed incorrect 'cdef class MSSpectrum:' declaration
   - Fixed get_data_dict() to use Python type introspection instead of
     Cython cdef DataValue (which doesn't work in def methods)
   - Changed precursor_charge dtype to int16 (can be negative)
   - Improved documentation and code formatting

3. _dataframes.py:
   - Added _MSSpectrumDF wrapper class that provides get_df() method
   - get_df() calls get_data_dict() and converts to pandas DataFrame
   - Added MSSpectrum and PeakSpectrum aliases for the DF wrapper class
   - Follows same pattern as _MSChromatogramDF

4. Tests:
   - Comprehensive tests for get_data_dict() covering basic spectra,
     ion mobility, precursors, meta values, empty spectra
   - Tests for get_df() DataFrame export functionality
   - Fixed NaN comparison issues (use np.isnan instead of ==)

author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit message:
Fix iBAQ normalization silently skipped for protein groups (issue #8466)

The root cause was an accession mismatch between prot_quant_ keys and
ProteinHit accessions:
- transferPeptideDataToProteins_() populates prot_quant_ using LEADER
  accessions from getAccession_() + mapAccessionToLeader()
- performIbaqNormalization_() iterated over protein hits directly and
  looked up hit.getAccession() in prot_quant_
- When protein groups exist, non-leader hits would fail the lookup,
  silently skipping iBAQ normalization

The fix changes performIbaqNormalization_() to:
1. Build the same accession_to_leader mapping used elsewhere
2. Create a reverse leader_to_members mapping
3. Iterate over prot_quant_ entries (keyed by leaders) instead of hits
4. For each leader, find a sequence from the leader hit or any member

This ensures iBAQ normalization is applied correctly even when:
- Leader accession differs from protein hit accessions
- Only group member hits have sequences
- Complex protein inference produces group structures

Added two test cases that expose the bug:
- iBAQ with indistinguishable protein groups (leader present)
- iBAQ with missing leader protein hit (only members present)

commit message:
Add leader repair logic to updateProteinGroups

When protein groups are updated after filtering, the original leader
(first accession) may be removed. This commit adds logic to repair
the group leader by selecting the best-scoring remaining protein.

This is important because:
- Quantification aggregates abundance to the leader protein
- mzTab export uses the leader for main accession, description, taxid
- Downstream tools expect the first protein to be representative

Implementation:
- Added repairGroupLeaders_() helper function
- Builds accession->score map for O(1) score lookups
- Finds best-scoring protein in each group
- Swaps best to position 0 if not already there
- Respects higher_better score orientation

Added comprehensive tests for leader repair:
- Verifies leader is maintained when present
- Verifies new leader is selected when original is removed
- Tests explicit case where non-leader has best score

Add memory-efficient two-pass streaming approach to process large
transition TSV files with ~500MB peak memory instead of 15-20GB.

- StreamingTSVReader: Two-pass reader that builds collision index in
  pass 1 and streams groups in pass 2. Validates consecutive grouping.
- StreamingTSVWriter: Incremental writer for group-by-group output
- StreamingTransitionProcessor: Orchestrates streaming pipeline with
  filtering, top-N selection, and decoy generation with collision check

- Add -streaming_mode flag to OpenSwathAssayGenerator
- Requires TSV input/output, consecutive groups, no IPF support yet

- Only keeping one peptide group in memory at a time
- Using lightweight LightTransition structs (~136 bytes vs ~1000 bytes)
- Building collision index without storing all transitions

Instead of using Python wrapper classes in _dataframes.py to add DataFrame
export functionality, implement get_df() directly in the Cython addon files
alongside get_data_dict(). This simplifies the architecture by:

- Removing the "duck typing hack" of wrapper classes that override Cython classes
- Putting all DataFrame logic in one place (the Cython addon files)
- Making the code flow more straightforward

Changes:
- MSSpectrum.pyx: Added get_df()
- MSChromatogram.pyx: Added get_df()
- Mobilogram.pyx: Added get_df()
- MSExperiment.pyx: Added get_df_columns(), get_df(), get_ion_df(), get_massql_df()

- MRMTransitionGroupCP.pyx: New addon with get_chromatogram_df(), get_feature_df() methods

- Update _dataframes.py to use backwards-compatible wrapper functions that call the

  - Backwards-compatible wrapper functions

- Replace {bool: ...} dict keys with {type(True): ...} for same reason

author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
commit message:
Fix Light path decoy duplicate detection to use modified sequences

The Light path (generateDecoysLight) was incorrectly using unmodified
sequences for decoy duplicate detection, while the Heavy path uses
modified sequences (with UniMod annotations). This caused the Light
path to over-exclude decoys when multiple peptides had the same
unmodified sequence but different modifications.

Changes:
- Move modified sequence building before duplicate check in Light path
- Use full_decoy_sequence (with mods) instead of decoy_sequence for
  the duplicate detection key, matching Heavy path behavior at line 612
- Add OPENMS_LOG_DEBUG statements to Light path matching Heavy path

This fixes the issue where Light path generated significantly fewer
decoys (~75%) compared to Heavy path (~99%) for datasets with peptides
sharing the same unmodified sequence but different modifications.

commit message:
Performance optimizations for MRMAssay and MRMIonSeries

This commit implements several performance optimizations to improve
throughput for large-scale DIA assay library generation:

**Algorithm optimizations (P0):**
- getMatchingPeptidoforms_: O(n) → O(log n) using binary search
- getSwath_: O(n) → O(log n) using std::upper_bound
- isInSwath_: Fixed redundant getSwath_() call
- MRMIonSeries::getIonSeries: Incremental mass computation instead of
  repeated AASequence::getPrefix/getSuffix calls

**Lookup optimizations (P1):**
- detectingTransitions: Use std::set for O(log n) intensity lookup
- detectingTransitionsLight: Same optimization applied
- Removed unnecessary boost::lexical_cast<double>() conversions

**Memory optimizations:**
- Added reserve() calls to prevent vector reallocations in:
  - restrictTransitions/restrictTransitionsLight
  - detectingTransitions/detectingTransitionsLight
  - filterMinMaxTransitionsCompound
  - uisTransitions/uisTransitionsLight
- Removed redundant vector copies in generateTargetAssays_,
  generateDecoyAssays_, and Light variants by pre-sorting PeptideMaps

All optimizations preserve deterministic behavior (no unordered containers
used for iteration). Test coverage verified with 2385/2395 tests passing.

commit message:
Use unordered_map for compound_map lookups in Light path

Convert compound_map from std::map to std::unordered_map in all
Light-path functions where it is used only for lookup (never iterated):
- reannotateTransitionsLight_
- restrictTransitionsLight
- detectingTransitionsLight
- generateTargetAssaysLight_
- generateDecoyAssaysLight_

This provides O(1) average lookup instead of O(log n) for compound
ID lookups. Safe because compound_map is only accessed via .find()
and operator[], never iterated.

Note: std::set<double> for top_intensities is intentionally kept as
ordered set because:
1. Hashing doubles has edge cases (NaN, ±0.0, precision)
2. Set size is tiny (~6 elements), so O(log n) is negligible
3. Ordered comparison is more reliable across platforms

Add PeakFileOptions support to OnDiscMSExperiment (#8512)

* Add PeakFileOptions support to OnDiscMSExperiment

This enables users to set filtering options (m/z range, intensity range,
RT range, MS levels, etc.) for OnDiscMSExperiment, similar to how it works
for in-memory MSExperiment loading via FileHandler.

Changes:
- Added PeakFileOptions member and getOptions/setOptions methods
- Options are applied when loading metadata (RT range, MS levels filter)
- Options are applied when retrieving spectra (m/z, intensity filters)
- Options are applied when retrieving chromatograms (RT, intensity filters)
- Updated copy constructor to copy options
- Added pyOpenMS bindings for new methods
- Added comprehensive tests for the new functionality

* Optimize OnDiscMSExperiment to skip I/O for filtered spectra

When RT range or MS level filters are set, check metadata BEFORE loading
peak data. If a spectrum doesn't pass these filters, return it with
metadata but skip the expensive I/O operation to load peaks.

This allows efficient iteration over large files where only a subset
of spectra are needed based on RT or MS level criteria.

* Fix metadata loading to maintain index correspondence

Changed loadMetaData_() to always load ALL metadata without RT/MS level
filters. This ensures index correspondence between indexed_mzml_file_ and
meta_ms_experiment_ is maintained.

Filtering behavior for OnDiscMSExperiment:
- RT range and MS level filters are checked at retrieval time (skips I/O)
- Filtered spectra return with metadata but no peaks
- All indices are preserved (unlike in-memory loading where filtered
  spectra are removed from the container)

Also added comprehensive documentation explaining this behavior.

* feature: Add PeakFileOptions support to OnDiscMSExperiment (#8534)

* [FEATURE] Add FAIMS support to ProteomicsLFQ (#8478)

- Annotate peptide IDs with FAIMS_CV from spectrum data before feature
  detection, enabling proper per-CV filtering in FeatureFinderIdentificationAlgorithm
- Add documentation describing FAIMS support: automatic detection,
  per-CV processing, feature merging, and downstream alignment/linking

FAIMS data is now automatically handled:
1. FFI splits data by compensation voltage and processes each CV group
2. Features from different CVs representing the same analyte are merged
3. Merged features are aligned and linked based on RT and m/z

commit message:
Add portable hash functions for AASequence, EmpiricalFormula, and PeptideHit

Implement std::hash specializations for high-priority classes that enable
use in std::unordered_map/set. The hash functions are designed for:

- Portability: Uses FNV-1a algorithm instead of std::hash<std::string>
  which is implementation-defined. Same input produces same hash across
  platforms and compilers.

- Speed: FNV-1a is fast (XOR + multiply per byte), avoids expensive
  string conversions where possible.

- Low collisions: Uses proper hash combining with golden ratio mixing
  (same formula as boost::hash_combine).

Changes:
- Add CONCEPT/HashUtils.h with fnv1a_hash_bytes, fnv1a_hash_string,
  hash_combine, hash_int, and hash_char utilities
- Add std::hash<EmpiricalFormula> based on element atomic numbers + counts + charge
- Add std::hash<AASequence> based on residue codes + modifications + terminal mods
- Add PeptideHit::SequenceChargeHash and SequenceChargeEqual functors for
  identity-based hashing (sequence + charge)
- Add wrap-hash directives to Python wrappers for dict/set usage
- Add comprehensive tests for all hash functions

commit message:
Add some hash functions for python dict compatibility (#8576)

* Add hash function research document

Comprehensive analysis of existing hash implementations in OpenMS and
identification of classes that should have hash functions added.

Key findings:
- 9 existing hash implementations across 11 files
- 37+ core classes have operator== but lack hash functions
- AASequence and EmpiricalFormula are highest priority (performance-critical)
- Identified redundant data structures in TheoreticalSpectrumGenerator

* Add portable hash functions for AASequence, EmpiricalFormula, and PeptideHit

Implement std::hash specializations for high-priority classes that enable
use in std::unordered_map/set. The hash functions are designed for:

- Portability: Uses FNV-1a algorithm instead of std::hash<std::string>
  which is implementation-defined. Same input produces same hash across
  platforms and compilers.

- Speed: FNV-1a is fast (XOR + multiply per byte), avoids expensive
  string conversions where possible.

- Low collisions: Uses proper hash combining with golden ratio mixing
  (same formula as boost::hash_combine).

Changes:
- Add CONCEPT/HashUtils.h with fnv1a_hash_bytes, fnv1a_hash_string,
  hash_combine, hash_int, and hash_char utilities
- Add std::hash<EmpiricalFormula> based on element atomic numbers + counts + charge
- Add std::hash<AASequence> based on residue codes + modifications + terminal mods
- Add PeptideHit::SequenceChargeHash and SequenceChargeEqual functors for
  identity-based hashing (sequence + charge)
- Add wrap-hash directives to Python wrappers for dict/set usage
- Add comprehensive tests for all hash functions

* Improve hash function reproducibility and isotope handling

Changes:
- EmpiricalFormula: Use element symbols instead of atomic numbers to
  distinguish isotopes like (13)C vs C. Sort by symbol for reproducible
  hash across process runs.
- AASequence: Add explicit HashUtils.h include, remove unnecessary
  string copies, add ULL suffix to hex literals
- HashUtils: Add static_assert constraint to hash_int template,
  update documentation to clarify reproducibility guarantees

The hash functions are now:
- Reproducible across process runs on the same platform
- Isotope-aware (C and (13)C produce different hashes)
- Consistent with operator== for all classes

commit message:
Fix EMGScoring:init_mom default to match TOPP tool behavior

Change the default value of EMGScoring:init_mom from "false" to "true"
in both FeatureFinderAlgorithmMetaboIdent and FeatureFinderIdentificationAlgorithm.

This fixes issue #8550 where pyOpenMS users experienced different behavior
compared to TOPP tools (TOPPAS). The TOPP tools were overriding the algorithm
default to "true", causing a discrepancy that resulted in:
- Peak centroids being shifted
- Mass traces extended over peak tails
- Asymmetry model fitting errors

The method of moments (MOM) initialization provides better initial parameter
estimates for EMG fitting, which is why the TOPP tools were using it.

Also removes the now-redundant parameter overrides from FeatureFinderMetaboIdent
and ProteomicsLFQ TOPP tools.

Fixes #8550

commit message:
Fix isotope and adduct peak grouping for metabolites (#4483)

Addresses issues with mass trace grouping where different intensities led
to incorrect isotope and adduct peak grouping:

1. FeatureFindingMetabo isotope detection:
   - Changed RT overlap calculation from `overlap / max_length` to
     `overlap / min_length` (shorter trace's FWHM)
   - Increased overlap threshold from 70% to 95%, ensuring the shorter
     trace lies substantially within the longer trace
   - Added check that the apex of the longer (more intense) trace falls
     within the shorter trace's RT range

2. MetaboliteFeatureDeconvolution and FeatureDeconvolution adduct grouping:
   - Changed RT overlap calculation from `intersect_length / union_length`
     to `intersect_length / shorter_length`
   - This avoids penalizing weak signals that naturally produce shorter
     traces when paired with more intense signals

These changes improve grouping of isotope and adduct peaks when mass
traces have significantly different intensities, particularly for lower
intensity isotope peaks (+1 and higher).

commit message:
Fix conda activation race condition on Windows CI

On Windows, the CMake build process spawns multiple parallel subprocesses
(via Ninja). Each subprocess can trigger conda's shell hooks, causing
multiple simultaneous `conda activate` calls. This leads to race conditions
where processes fight over the same temporary files, resulting in errors:

- "The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process"
- "The system cannot find the file C:\Users\...\Temp\__conda_tmp_*.txt"
- "Failed to run 'conda activate base/ci'"

This is a known conda bug documented in:
- https://github.com/conda/conda/issues/8733
- https://github.com/conda/conda/issues/9911

The fix adds `conda init --reverse bash` after installing conda packages.
This removes conda's shell integration hooks from the bash profile. The
conda-installed packages (libarrow, libparquet) remain accessible via
$GITHUB_PATH which was already set earlier in the step.

Fixes: https://github.com/OpenMS/OpenMS/issues/8611

NativeIDParser class for better discoverability and maintainability.

- extractScanNumber(): Extract scan numbers using regex or CV accession
- getRegExFromNativeID(): Generate regex patterns for native ID formats
- isNativeID(): Check if a string is a native ID from vendor files

Supported native ID formats include Thermo (MS:1000768), Waters (MS:1000769),
WIFF (MS:1000770), Bruker (MS:1000771-73, MS:1000775-76), Agilent (MS:1001508),
and generic formats (MS:1000774, MS:1000777, MS:1001530).

SpectrumLookup methods now delegate to NativeIDParser, maintaining backward
compatibility while guiding users to the new class via @deprecated/@see
documentation.

Includes comprehensive unit tests covering all supported formats and edge
cases, plus PyOpenMS bindings for Python accessibility.

commit message:
Replace CITATIONS.md with CITATION.cff for full GitHub citability

GitHub's "Cite this repository" feature works best with CITATION.cff
(Citation File Format) rather than CITATIONS.md. While GitHub recognizes
both file types, only CITATION.cff enables:
- Automatic APA formatted citation generation
- Automatic BibTeX formatted citation generation
- Machine-readable citation metadata

Add ProForma v2 parser implementation

Implement full support for the HUPO-PSI ProForma 2.0 standard for
representing peptidoforms (modified peptide sequences).

New components:
- ProFormaData.h: AST data structures using std::variant for
  polymorphic modification types (CvAccession, NamedMod, MassDelta,
  FormulaTag, GlycanComposition, InfoTag, CationTag)

- ProFormaParser: Recursive descent parser with comprehensive error
  reporting including line/column positions
- ProFormaWriter: Serialization back to ProForma string format
- ProFormaError: Exception classes with detailed error context
- MonosaccharideDB: Database for glycan monosaccharide data

Supported ProForma features:
- CV accessions (UNIMOD, MOD, RESID, XLMOD, GNO)
- Named modifications with spaces (e.g., "half cystine")
- Mass deltas with optional database prefixes (U:, Obs:)
- Formula tags with isotope notation and charge
- Glycan compositions
- N/C-terminal modifications (single and multiple)
- Unlocalised modifications with multiplicity
- Labile modifications
- Global modifications (isotope labels and fixed mods with targets)
- Cross-link labels with localization scores
- Modification alternatives
- Ambiguous regions and modified ranges
- Charge states (simple and adduct notation)
- Multiple chains (// separator) and chimeric spectra (+ separator)
- Gene/protein prefixes
- INFO tags and position constraints

Test coverage:
- 49 explicit test sections covering all features
- Integration tests using 176 positive and 22 negative test cases
  from the official HUPO-PSI ProForma test suite

preserve deterministic iteration order.

- data_page_size: Granularity within row groups (default 1MB)

defaults to ZSTD which is optimal for MS data.

empty binary arrays (encodedLength="0", empty <binary> tags). This

commit message:
Fix wrap-doc validator to properly end blocks after blank lines

The wrap-doc validator was incorrectly treating comments like "# private"
or "# protected" that appeared after blank lines as wrap-doc continuation
lines. This caused false positives in 7 pxd files (ModificationsDB, RNaseDB,
ElementDB, Param, RibonucleotideDB, CrossLinksDB, ProteaseDB).

The fix adds tracking of blank lines within wrap-doc blocks. When a blank
line is followed by a single-space comment (like "# private"), the validator
now correctly ends the wrap-doc block instead of flagging it as a format error.

This allows valid multi-paragraph wrap-doc blocks while properly separating
wrap-doc content from subsequent unrelated comments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit message:
Make wrap-doc extraction stricter to match validation rules

Address CodeRabbit review comment: the extract_wrap_doc_from_pxd()
function was accepting single-space continuations "# " which is
inconsistent with the validator that requires two spaces "#  ".

Changes:
- Only accept "#  " (hash + exactly 2 spaces) as continuation lines
- Accept "#" (just hash) for blank lines in docstrings
- Remove the branch that accepted single-space "# " continuations
- Update regex from r'\s*#\s?' to r'\s*#\s{2}' for strict matching
- Add proper break for wrap directive boundaries

This makes extraction consistent with validation and prevents
accidentally extracting unrelated comments as wrap-doc content.

commit message:
Fix UniqueIdGenerator seed collision in parallel pipelines

Mix process ID into the seed to ensure different seeds for parallel
processes started at the same microsecond. This prevents duplicate
UniqueIds when multiple TOPP tools run simultaneously in a pipeline,
which was causing "FeatureHandle exists twice in ConsensusMap" errors
in QualityControl.

The seed now combines:
- Microsecond-resolution time (existing)
- Process ID shifted to upper 32 bits (new)

Added SysInfo::getProcessId() as a cross-platform wrapper for getpid().

commit message:
Fix pyarrow filesystem conflict with cached LocalFileSystem instances

Apply the "ultrahack" solution from apache/arrow#44696 that patches
pyarrow's _resolve_filesystem_and_path to reuse cached LocalFileSystem
instances instead of creating new ones.

Key improvements:
- Create and cache LocalFileSystem instances before C++ Arrow loads
- Verify pyarrow internal APIs exist before patching (version compat)
- Exit early if C++ already registered (can't help in that case)
- Cache miss creates new instance on demand

This prevents the "Attempted to register factory for scheme 'file'"
error when both pyarrow and OpenMS Arrow C++ are present, without
requiring users to modify their code.

See: https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/44696#issuecomment-3532192904

commit message:
Add mass calculation support for ProForma peptidoforms

Add methods to calculate monoisotopic mass and m/z directly from
Peptidoform and PeptidoformIon ASTs without requiring AASequence
conversion.

New API:
- canCalculateMass(Peptidoform/PeptidoformIon): Check if mass can be calculated
- getMassCalculationIssues(): Get detailed issues preventing mass calculation
- getMonoWeight(Peptidoform/PeptidoformIon): Calculate neutral monoisotopic mass
- getMZ(PeptidoformIon): Calculate m/z using ion's charge state
- getMZ(Peptidoform, charge): Calculate m/z at given charge

Features:
- Works with resolved modifications, mass deltas, and formulas
- Properly handles cross-links (counts cross-linker mass only once)
- Supports multi-chain peptidoforms and chimeric spectra
- Includes unlocalised and labile modifications in mass
- Applies global modifications to matching residues

Cross-link mass calculation uses the same mass values as CrossLinksDB
(e.g., DSS/BS3 = 138.06807961 Da).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

default object file section limit (65,535 sections), causing build

format that supports more sections.

warnings from generated Cython code.

commit message:
fix: handle empty GENE table in PQP file reading (#8687)

When reading PQP files, the code previously checked if the GENE table
exists but not if it contained any rows. An empty GENE table with
INNER JOINs would return zero rows, causing all peptide/transition
data to be lost ("no transitions" error).

This fix adds a row count check after verifying table existence,
treating an empty GENE table the same as a non-existent one.

Fixes #8687
Related to #8683

feat: Add digestWithVariants method to PEFFEntry

Add method to generate all variant peptide combinations from enzymatic
digestion. The method accepts a ProteaseDigestion object (allowing any
enzyme like Trypsin, Chymotrypsin, etc.) and generates all 2^k
combinations of simple variants within each peptide, where k is the
number of variants in that peptide's span.

protein-level combinations, making it tractable for proteins with many
variants like P53 (1000+ variants).

commit message:
(feat,openswath): Write multi-run support: register multiple RUNs in OSW and sqMass; wire per-file run_id for extraction

Add multi-run plumbing so multiple independent input experiment files (multiple mzML / SRM inputs)
can be processed into a single OSW and a single sqMass while preserving per-file RUN bookkeeping.
New/changed APIs:
Internal::MzMLSqliteHandler::setRunId(UInt64) — allow changing the run id used by the sqMass handler at runtime.
MSDataSqlConsumer::addRun(const String & filename, UInt64 run_id) — insert a RUN entry into the sqMass and mark that a run has been written.
MSDataSqlConsumer::setRunId(UInt64) — change the current run id used for subsequent chromatogram/spectrum writes.
Guard MSDataSqlConsumer destructor to avoid writing a duplicate RUN row if runs were already registered via addRun.
OpenSwathOSWWriter was previously extended (header change) to allow multi-run registration (addRun, setRunId); the workflow is now wired to use it.
Workflow wiring:
OpenSwathWorkflow.cpp:
Register a unique run_id per unique input filename and call oswwriter.addRun(run_id, filename).
When a sqMass consumer is in use, call MSDataSqlConsumer::addRun(...) as well so the sqMass gets RUN entries.
Before extracting each group's swath maps (grouped by originating filename via swath_map_sources), set the current run id in both the OSW writer and the sqMass consumer (setRunId) so FEATURES and CHROMATOGRAM rows are written with the correct RUN_ID.
Behavioral effect:
Multiple input experiment mzMLs are treated as independent runs, can be processed in a single tool invocation, and the resulting .osw and .sqMass will contain one RUN row per input file with features/chromatograms linked to the proper RUN_ID.

feat: Add generatePeptides method with variable modification support

Refactor peptide generation to support additional variable modifications
(like Oxidation from sample handling) on top of PEFF annotations.

New method `generatePeptides()` provides a complete workflow:
1. Enzymatic digestion
2. PEFF variant enumeration (position-specific substitutions)
3. PEFF modification enumeration (position-specific PTMs)
4. Additional variable modifications via ModifiedPeptideGenerator

combinatorial logic from digestion.

```cpp
std::vector<String> sample_mods = {"Oxidation (M)", "Deamidated (N)"};
auto peptides = entry.generatePeptides(
    digestor,
    sample_mods,     // additional variable mods
    2,               // max 2 variable mods per peptide
    6, 40,           // length range
    true,            // include reference
    true,            // include PEFF variants
    true             // include PEFF modifications
);
```

commit message:
feat(pyOpenMS2): Add nanobind-based Python bindings infrastructure with libclang support

Add pyOpenMS2, a nanobind-based replacement for pyOpenMS that provides:

- Generator framework that parses existing .pxd files and emits nanobind C++ code
- Support for libclang-based C++ header parsing for accurate type information
- Custom type casters for OpenMS types (String, DPosition, DataValue, STL containers)
- Multi-module split (8 modules) for parallel compilation
- Pure Python addon system for extending bound classes

Key components:
- generator/pxd_parser.py: Parses .pxd declaration files
- generator/cpp_parser.py: Uses libclang for accurate C++ signatures
- generator/nanobind_emitter.py: Generates nanobind binding code
- generator/nanobind_emitter_v2.py: Enhanced emitter using libclang info
- bindings/type_casters/: Custom nanobind type casters

The libclang integration provides:
- Accurate const qualifier detection
- Static method identification
- Pure virtual (abstract class) detection
- Exact parameter and return types

Usage:
  cmake -DPYOPENMS2_USE_LIBCLANG=ON ...
  cmake --build . --target pyopenms2_generate

feat(pyOpenMS2): improve nanobind emitter with feature parity enhancements

- Add SKIP_CLASSES for classes with incomplete types or missing statics
- Add SKIP_METHODS for methods with type signature mismatches
- Add VECTOR_INHERITED_METHODS to skip private base class methods
- Add SPECIAL_METHODS with C++ lambdas for get_peaks, set_peaks, etc.
- Add __repr__, __len__, __iter__, __getitem__ for container classes
- Update _normalize_type to handle OpenMS typedefs and enums
- Use static_cast for const method overloads (nanobind compatibility)
- Add pxd_to_merged() to use v2 emitter without libclang

The minimal test (Peak1D, MSSpectrum) now compiles and passes:
- get_peaks/set_peaks work with Python lists
- __len__, __iter__, __getitem__ work for iteration
- __repr__ provides nice representations

feat(pyOpenMS2): core classes fully working with lambda-based bindings

Major improvements to the nanobind-based Python bindings:

  that occur when C++ has overloads not declared in .pxd files
- Fix pxd_parser to handle multi-word return types (unsigned int, long long)
- Fix pxd_parser to handle parameters without names (like "unsigned int")
- Add core_only mode to bind well-tested classes first (Peak1D, Peak2D,
  ChromatogramPeak, MSSpectrum, MSChromatogram)
- Make each sub-module a standalone NB_MODULE for proper multi-module loading
- Update __init__.py to import all sub-modules dynamically
- Add C++ reserved keyword checking for parameter names
- Expand type normalization with many more OpenMS types

Working classes:
- Peak1D: getMZ, setMZ, getIntensity, setIntensity, __repr__
- Peak2D: getMZ, setMZ, getRT, setRT, getIntensity, setIntensity, __repr__

std::vector<OpenSwath::SwathMap> because it couldn't resolve types
from headers that depend on Qt or OpenSwathAlgo.

  (it's in OpenSwath:: namespace, not OpenMS::)
- Enable SwathFileConsumer classes and AnnotatedMSRun (previously skipped
  due to type mismatch errors)

commit message:
Add nested type support to libclang parser

The cpp_parser now detects and processes nested classes/structs inside
parent classes. Nested types are exposed with flattened names matching
the pxd convention (e.g., ModifiedPeptideGenerator_MapToResidueType).

Key changes:
- _process_class() and _process_class_template() now accept out_classes
  and parent_class_name parameters for recursive nested type collection
- _process_class_members() detects CLASS_DECL and STRUCT_DECL children
  and processes them as nested types with flattened names
- Cache version bumped to 4 for the new parsing behavior
- ModifiedPeptideGenerator re-enabled (now works with nested MapToResidueType)

Result: 504 merged classes (was 484), +20 nested types now available.

commit message:
Add C++11 scoped enum (enum class) support to generator

- Detect scoped enums via libclang's is_scoped_enum() method
- Track scoped enums in CppHeaderParser._scoped_enums set
- Mark enums as is_scoped=True in merge_with_pxd when matched
- Conditionally generate .export_values() only for regular enums
  (scoped enums keep their values scoped as intended)
- Auto-attach enums to classes by file name when not explicitly
  attached (e.g., enums in IMTypes.pxd attach to IMTypes class)

This ensures correct nanobind binding generation for both regular
C++ enums (which export values to parent scope) and C++11 enum
class types (which keep values scoped).

  during parsing

  NumberOfEntries) with warnings

  (single AA substitution must use VariantSimple)
- Reject semicolon-leading lines per spec section 3.3.3
- Write AltAC as single key with parenthesized list to avoid duplicate
  keys

- Add mandatory field validation warnings on write
- Remove db_date from PEFFDatabaseMetadata (not in spec)

- Add PEFFCustomKeyDef struct and parsing/writing support

commit message:
Fix template instance generation and pxd parser bugs

- Fix template classes (MRMTransitionGroup, Matrix, BilinearInterpolation)
  getting 0 methods: libclang finds them but can't enumerate template
  methods, so fall back to pxd declarations when libclang has 0 methods
- Move template instance check before SKIP_CLASSES so template bases
  in SKIP_CLASSES don't block their instantiations
- Fix pxd parser multi-line detection: parentheses in inline comments
  no longer trigger continuation
- Add word-boundary regex for template param substitution to prevent
  partial matches (e.g., libclang's 'Key' matching inside pxd's 'KeyType')
- Store pxd_template_params on MergedClass to handle libclang/pxd

commit message:
Fix template specialization false-positive incomplete type detection

libclang marks implicit template specializations (e.g., DBoundingBox<2>)
as incomplete because the instantiation isn't a definition cursor node,
even though the template class is fully defined. This caused methods like
ConvexHull2D::getBoundingBox (returning DBoundingBox<2>) to be skipped.

Add _KNOWN_COMPLETE_TEMPLATES whitelist in cpp_parser.py and check for
template arguments before flagging a type as incomplete. Remove the now-
redundant ConvexHull2D SPECIAL_METHODS entry.

commit message:
Fix rv_policy for reference returns in templates, operator[], and ExposedVector containers

Add rv_policy::reference_internal for three code paths that were returning
C++ references without telling nanobind, causing copies instead of mutable
references:

1. Template instance methods returning T& or T* now get rv_policy detection
2. Non-vector container __getitem__ (operator[]) now detects reference returns
   and applies reference_internal with explicit return type
3. ExposedVector-based containers (ConsensusMap, FeatureMap, MSExperiment)
   infer element type for operator[] when libclang can't see the inherited method

Also adds regression tests for mutable reference returns and fixes the test
conftest.py build path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit message:
feat: Add PEFF (PSI Extended FASTA Format) file support (#8690)

* feat: Add PEFF (PSI Extended FASTA Format) file support

Implements full PEFF format support for reading and writing protein
sequence files with rich annotations.

New features:
- PEFFFile class with batch (load/store) and streaming APIs
- Support for all PEFF annotation types:
  - Modifications (PSI-MOD, UNIMOD, custom)
  - Simple variants (single amino acid substitutions)
  - Complex variants (insertions, deletions, multi-residue changes)
  - Processed regions (signal peptides, transit peptides, etc.)
  - Proteoforms (ProForma notation)
- Database metadata parsing (version, name, prefix, decoy flag, etc.)
- AASequence integration methods:
  - getSequence() - unmodified sequence
  - getModifiedSequence() - with modifications applied
  - getVariantSequences() - all variant sequences
  - getProcessedSequence() - mature protein without signal peptide
- File type detection via isPEFFFile()
- pyOpenMS bindings with convenience methods

Files:
- PEFFFile.h/cpp - Core implementation
- PEFFFile.pxd/pyx - Python bindings
- PEFFFile_test.cpp - Unit tests
- Test data files (*.peff)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: Address PR review comments for PEFF support

- Fix FileTypes_test to expect correct count (39 READABLE, 62 total)
- Add PEFF test to FileHandler_test and FileTypes_test
- Fix PEFFFile_test.peff \Length=50 -> \Length=49 to match sequence
- Fix PEFFFile_test.cpp expected sequence_length to 49
- Fix getModifiedSequence() docs (doesn't throw, logs and skips)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Implement PEFFFile::toProForma() conversion

Implements full ProForma notation generation from PEFF entries:
- Localised modifications: placed after the amino acid they modify
- Unlocalised modifications (position 0): encoded as <?[mod]> prefix
- Supports CV accessions (UNIMOD:, MOD:) and named modifications
- Multiple modifications at same position supported

Added comprehensive tests:
- Single and multiple modifications
- Unlocalised and mixed modifications
- Named modifications without accessions
- Round-trip verification with ProForma parser

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Fix getModifiedSequence() to try accession first, then name
  (previously extracted unimod_id but never used it)
- Remove unused formatModifications_() helper function
- Add Python binding overload for getProcessedSequence() default param
- Fix test to properly access ProForma variant elements

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Add annotation identifier support to PEFF parser

Add support for the PEFF HasAnnotationIdentifiers feature, which prefixes
annotations with unique IDs in the format `annotationID:position`.

Changes:
- Add annotation_id field to PEFFModification, PEFFVariantSimple,
  PEFFVariantComplex, and PEFFProcessedRegion structs
- Add has_annotation_identifiers flag to PEFFDatabaseMetadata
- Update parse functions to detect and extract annotation IDs
- Update format functions to output annotation IDs when present
- Extend getVariantSequences() to optionally include complex variants

Example formats supported:
- Without IDs: \ModResPsi=(10|UNIMOD:35|Oxidation)
- With IDs: \ModResPsi=(0:10|MOD:00046|Phosphorylation)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Add UniProt-style PEFF keywords and DisulfideBond support

Add missing PEFF 1.0 specification keywords found in UniProt examples:

Entry keywords:
- \DbUniqueId - Unique database identifier
- \ID - Entry identifier (e.g., NPM_HUMAN)
- \OX - Shorthand for NcbiTaxId
- \AltAC - Alternative accessions
- \DisulfideBond - Disulfide bond annotations

Header keywords:
- # Conversion - Conversion notes
- # SpecificValue - Custom value type definitions
- Multiple # GeneralComment lines (changed to vector)

Also includes DRY refactoring: extract annotation ID parsing into
helper function (was duplicated 4 times).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: Add real UniProt P53 PEFF test file

Downloaded from EBI Proteins API variation endpoint:
https://www.ebi.ac.uk/proteins/api/variation/P04637?format=peff

Tests parsing of:
- Real UniProt PEFF format with 1000+ variants
- Stop codon variants (*)
- Bracketed variant sources like [ExAC][gnomAD]
- Multiple GeneralComment lines

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Add digestWithVariants method to PEFFEntry

Add method to generate all variant peptide combinations from enzymatic
digestion. The method accepts a ProteaseDigestion object (allowing any
enzyme like Trypsin, Chymotrypsin, etc.) and generates all 2^k
combinations of simple variants within each peptide, where k is the
number of variants in that peptide's span.

This per-peptide approach is more efficient than generating all 2^n
protein-level combinations, making it tractable for proteins with many
variants like P53 (1000+ variants).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Add modification support to digestWithVariants

Extend digestWithVariants to generate modification combinations in
addition to variant combinations. New parameters:
- include_variants: enable/disable variant combination generation
- include_modifications: enable/disable modification combination generation

For each peptide with k variants and m modifications, generates up to
2^(k+m) combinations. Modifications with unknown positions (position==0)
are skipped. Modification application uses ModificationsDB for lookup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: Address PR review comments

- Add safeguard for combinatorial explosion in digestWithVariants
  (limit to 20 elements = ~1M combinations max per peptide)
- Add annotation_id field to Python bindings for PEFFModification,
  PEFFVariantSimple, PEFFVariantComplex, PEFFProcessedRegion
- Add has_annotation_identifiers field to PEFFDatabaseMetadata binding
- Replace bare except clause with except Exception in addon

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Add generatePeptides method with variable modification support

Refactor peptide generation to support additional variable modifications
(like Oxidation from sample handling) on top of PEFF annotations.

New method `generatePeptides()` provides a complete workflow:
1. Enzymatic digestion
2. PEFF variant enumeration (position-specific substitutions)
3. PEFF modification enumeration (position-specific PTMs)
4. Additional variable modifications via ModifiedPeptideGenerator

Also adds helper method `enumeratePEFFModifications_()` to separate
combinatorial logic from digestion.

Example usage:
```cpp
std::vector<String> sample_mods = {"Oxidation (M)", "Deamidated (N)"};
auto peptides = entry.generatePeptides(
    digestor,
    sample_mods,     // additional variable mods
    2,               // max 2 variable mods per peptide
    6, 40,           // length range
    true,            // include reference
    true,            // include PEFF variants
    true             // include PEFF modifications
);
```

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: Add fixed modification support to generatePeptides

The generatePeptides method now accepts both fixed_mods and variable_mods
parameters, enabling complete sample handling modification workflows:
- Fixed mods (e.g., Carbamidomethyl) are applied to all compatible residues
- Variable mods (e.g., Oxidation) generate combinatorial forms

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Implements pure Python versions of digestWithVariants() and generatePeptides()

return type directly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Reduce from 299 to 154 lines by removing verbose docstrings,
dead code, and unnecessary nesting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Change getVariantSequences, digestWithVariants, and generatePeptides to use

without custom type converters.

Changes C++ API to use std::string instead of OpenMS::String for:

- Input modification name parameters (fixed_mods, variable_mods) in generatePeptides

This enables automatic Python str ↔ C++ string conversion via autowrap's
libcpp_utf8_string/libcpp_utf8_output_string types, so Python bindings
now return str instead of bytes for descriptions.

When include_reference=false and there are PEFF modifications,

* fix: PEFF spec compliance fixes for parsing, writing, and validation

Address multiple PEFF specification compliance issues:

- Write modifications under type-specific keys (ModResPsi, ModResUnimod,
  ModRes) instead of all under ModRes, preserving round-trip semantics
- Support comma-separated positions in modification tuples per spec
  sections 3.3.10-3.3.12
- Implement escape-aware splitting for pipes and parentheses, handling
  \|, \\, \(, \) escape sequences in values
- Add ProteoformDb header field (is_proteoform_db) with parsing/writing
- Add DisulfideBond annotation_id field and extract annotation IDs

Implements full PEFF format support for reading and writing protein
sequence files with rich annotations.

New features:
- PEFFFile class with batch (load/store) and streaming APIs
- Support for all PEFF annotation types:
  - Modifications (PSI-MOD, UNIMOD, custom)
  - Simple variants (single amino acid substitutions)
  - Complex variants (insertions, deletions, multi-residue changes)
  - Processed regions (signal peptides, transit peptides, etc.)
  - Proteoforms (ProForma notation)
- Database metadata parsing (version, name, prefix, decoy flag, etc.)
- AASequence integration methods:
  - getSequence() - unmodified sequence
  - getModifiedSequence() - with modifications applied
  - getVariantSequences() - all variant sequences
  - getProcessedSequence() - mature protein without signal peptide
- File type detection via isPEFFFile()
- pyOpenMS bindings with convenience methods

Files:
- PEFFFile.h/cpp - Core implementation
- PEFFFile.pxd/pyx - Python bindings
- PEFFFile_test.cpp - Unit tests
- Test data files (*.peff)

* feat: Add digestWithVariants method to PEFFEntry

Add method to generate all variant peptide combinations from enzymatic
digestion. The method accepts a ProteaseDigestion object (allowing any
enzyme like Trypsin, Chymotrypsin, etc.) and generates all 2^k
combinations of simple variants within each peptide, where k is the
number of variants in that peptide's span.

This per-peptide approach is more efficient than generating all 2^n
protein-level combinations, making it tractable for proteins with many
variants like P53 (1000+ variants).

are skipped. Modification application uses ModificationsDB for lookup.

* feat: Add generatePeptides method with variable modification support

(like Oxidation from sample handling) on top of PEFF annotations.

New method `generatePeptides()` provides a complete workflow:

2. PEFF variant enumeration (position-specific substitutions)
3. PEFF modification enumeration (position-specific PTMs)
4. Additional variable modifications via ModifiedPeptideGenerator

```cpp
    digestor,

    6, 40,           // length range

);
```

commit message:
refactor: use sigmoid reparameterization instead of penalty for RT bounds

Replace the virtual boundary penalty approach with sigmoid
reparameterization to enforce RT bounds in EmgFitter1D. This maps the
RT parameter to unconstrained space via logit/sigmoid transforms,
guaranteeing the optimizer never evaluates RT outside the data range
without needing penalty tuning or post-hoc clamping.

Add PSM DataFrame export from PeptideIdentificationList following QPX schema (#8632)

* Add get_psm_df() export for PeptideIdentificationList following QPX schema

Adds three new methods to PeptideIdentificationList:
- get_psm_df(): Export PSMs as DataFrame with QPX schema columns
- psm_to_arrow(): Export PSMs as Apache Arrow Table
- get_psm_columns(): Return available column names

Key features:
- Exports ALL hits by default (unlike get_df() which only exports rank 0)
- Includes: sequence, peptidoform, precursor_charge, observed_mz, calculated_mz,
  rt, scan, spectrum_reference, is_decoy, score, score_type, rank,
  protein_accessions, modifications, posterior_error_probability,
  additional_scores, ion_mobility
- Optional fragment ion annotations (mz_array, intensity_array, charge_array,
  annotation_array) via include_peak_annotations=True

commit message:
Fix Windows wheel build: remove PYOPENMS_SRC_DIR from Cython include path

The addition of PYOPENMS_SRC_DIR to Cython's include directories was
causing 'String' redeclared errors on Windows. When the source directory
is in the include path, Cython finds both the original String.pxd (with
cdef cppclass String) and the autowrap-generated _pyopenms_N.pxd (with
cdef class String), treating them as conflicting declarations.

Revert to using only autowrap's generated include directories.

commit message:
Add Parquet support for XIC chromatogram output (C++ core)

This PR adds support for OpenSWATH chromatogram Parquet files (.xic).
It introduces a Parquet writer for chromatograms, a reader with filtering
and predicate pushdown, and test coverage including TOPP regression checks.

The schema uses a similar (expanded) schema that was implemented in
PyProphet to convert the sqMass chromatograms to parquet. Adding parquet
xic output directly to OpenSwathWorkflow skips the additional extra
conversion step, and provides storage benefits from using parquet
compared to sqMass.

Additions:
- MSChromatogramParquetConsumer: writes .xic Parquet files with a
  PyProphet-compatible schema (metadata + compressed RT/intensity arrays)
- XICParquetFile: reads .xic files with filter expressions; supports
  multi-file input and Arrow Dataset predicate pushdown with compute fallback
- ParquetFilter: typed, chainable Parquet filter builder for predicate pushdown
- TextExporter: now supports .xic input, exporting summary or exploded
  TSV/CSV/TXT for testable text output
- OpenSwathWorkflow: added -out_chrom_ext xic option for Parquet output
- Unit and TOPP tests for the new functionality

Note: Python bindings will be added in a follow-up PR.

Based on work from PR #8725 by @singjc.

commit message:
Add pyOpenMS bindings for XICParquetFile

This PR adds Python bindings for reading XIC data from Parquet files,
enabling integration with pandas, pyarrow, and pyopenms_viz.

Additions:
- XICParquetFile Python bindings with:
  - list-of-files constructor support
  - get_data_dict, get_chromatograms, to_df, to_arrow
  - get_analyte_dict, get_analyte_df, get_run_dict, get_run_df
  - df_columns for column discovery
  - Filter expressions with predicate pushdown support
- ParquetFilter/ParquetFilterBuilder Python bindings for typed filter construction
- ParquetQuery/ChromatogramQuery for chainable querying
- Unit tests for Python bindings

Example usage:
```python
import pyopenms as poms
import glob

files = glob.glob('*.xic')
xic_h = poms.XICParquetFile(files)
xic_h.get_chromatograms(filter="precursor_id=1318 & annotation=y3^1").plot(
    kind="chromatogram", x="rt", y="intensity", by="source_file"
)
```

Depends on PR #8737 (C++ core).
Based on work from PR #8725 by @singjc.

Parse standalone function declarations in .pxd files with C++ qualified names
(e.g., `bool isPEFFFile "OpenMS::PEFFFile::isPEFFFile" (...)`) and wrap them
as static methods on their associated classes.

Changes:
- pxd_parser.py: Add cpp_name field to Method, detect standalone functions,
  extract target class from namespace, attach as static methods
- cpp_parser.py: Add cpp_name field to MergedMethod, propagate through merging
- nanobind_emitter.py: Use cpp_name in _generate_static_method() when available

This enables wrapping functions like PEFFFile::isPEFFFile, PEFFFile::toProForma,
and PEFFEntry::fromFASTAEntry as static methods on their respective classes.

[pyOpenMS] Add Python bindings for XICParquetFile (#8738)

* Add pyOpenMS bindings for XICParquetFile

This PR adds Python bindings for reading XIC data from Parquet files,
enabling integration with pandas, pyarrow, and pyopenms_viz.

Additions:
- XICParquetFile Python bindings with:
  - list-of-files constructor support
  - get_data_dict, get_chromatograms, to_df, to_arrow
  - get_analyte_dict, get_analyte_df, get_run_dict, get_run_df
  - df_columns for column discovery
  - Filter expressions with predicate pushdown support
- ParquetFilter/ParquetFilterBuilder Python bindings for typed filter construction
- ParquetQuery/ChromatogramQuery for chainable querying
- Unit tests for Python bindings

Example usage:
```python
import pyopenms as poms
import glob

files = glob.glob('*.xic')
xic_h = poms.XICParquetFile(files)
xic_h.get_chromatograms(filter="precursor_id=1318 & annotation=y3^1").plot(
    kind="chromatogram", x="rt", y="intensity", by="source_file"
)
```

Depends on PR #8737 (C++ core).
Based on work from PR #8725 by @singjc.

with the autowrap-generated cdef class wrapper on Windows. The addon
uses `isinstance(x, String)` which requires the Python type (cdef class),
not the cppclass. The cdef class is already available in scope when
the addon is injected into the generated module.

commit message:
Refactor/osw calibration (#8743)

* Add CalibrationWorkflow integration for RT transformation in OpenSwathWorkflow

- Introduced CalibrationWorkflow for modular calibration of RT, m/z, and ion mobility.
- Replaced manual calibration logic with a single call to CalibrationWorkflow, simplifying the calibration process.
- Added support for loading existing RT transformation files, skipping calibration if provided.
- Updated configuration mapping from TOPP parameters to CalibrationConfig for better parameter management.
- Enhanced logging for clarity during calibration steps and outcomes.
- Included new header file CalibrationWorkflow.h in OpenSwathWorkflow.cpp.

* Refactor CalibrationWorkflow for iRT Calibration

- Removed the dependency on a transformation file for calibration, allowing for a more flexible approach using iRT experiments.
- Introduced a new IrtExperiments structure to manage linear and nonlinear iRT data.
- Added a strategy for preparing iRT experiments based on static files or sampling from a full transition library.
- Updated performCalibration, performLinearCalibration, and performLinearThenNonlinearCalibration methods to utilize the new iRT structure and parameters.
- Enhanced logging for better traceability during calibration processes.
- Removed redundant validation functions and streamlined configuration checks.
- Improved handling of estimated extraction windows based on new parameters.

* Refactor OpenSwathWorkflow to integrate CalibrationWorkflow parameters for iRT calibration

* Update iRT calibration handling in OpenSwathWorkflow and CalibrationWorkflow

* Add nonlinear RT extraction window parameter to CalibrationWorkflow and OpenSwathWorkflow

* Add nonlinear outlier detection parameter to CalibrationWorkflow

* Add ion mobility transformation handling and debug level parameter to CalibrationWorkflow

* Add percentile parameters for m/z and ion mobility window estimation in CalibrationWorkflow and SwathMapMassCorrection

* Update percentile parameters for m/z and ion mobility window estimation in CalibrationWorkflow and SwathMapMassCorrection

* Filter parameters for CalibrationWorkflow by excluding MassIMCorrection and RTNormalization settings

* Refactor extraction parameters handling in OpenSwathWorkflow to create fresh copies for each run, preventing parameter carry-over.

* Refactor logging in CalibrationWorkflow to use debug level instead of info level and add progress indicators for calibration steps

* Remove progress indicators for retention time normalization in OpenSwathWorkflow

* Refactor logging in OpenSwathWorkflow to use warning level for existing RT transformation and remove unnecessary info logs

* Refactor logging in CalibrationWorkflow to use debug level instead of info level for calibration steps

* Remove transition_exp parameter from calibration functions in CalibrationWorkflow

* Centralize RT normalization and data normalization logic in CalibrationWorkflow

* Refactor OpenSwathWorkflow to remove legacy estimated-window getters/setters and use CalibrationWorkflow for RT normalization

* Refactor OpenSwathWorkflow to remove OpenSwathCalibrationWorkflow and centralize RT/m/z normalization logic in CalibrationWorkflow

* Refactor CalibrationWorkflow to remove logging statements for linear and nonlinear calibration steps

* Add unit test for CalibrationWorkflow data normalization functionality

* Add NULL_TRANSFORMATION strategy to IrtStrategy enum and update calibration logic

* Implement feature X to enhance user experience and fix bug Y in module Z

* Enhance RT transformation loading by using FileHandler and fitting model parameters to match original implementation

* Remove redundant file processing log message in OpenSwathWorkflow

* Refactor CalibrationWorkflow and OpenSwathBase to centralize calibration logic and improve code clarity

* Remove unused mz_correction_function option and related code in OpenSwathWorkflow

* Remove outlierMethod option and related validation from parameters

* Remove unused nonlinear parameters and enhance outlier detection method descriptions in CalibrationWorkflow

* Refactor CalibrationWorkflow parameters for clarity and remove unused options

* Add unit test for CalibrationWorkflow::performCalibration method with detailed chromatogram simulations

* refactor,test: refactor irt input list for run-specific and add TOPP test for multi mzml and multi linear iRT input

* refactor: remove deprecated OpenSwathCalibrationWorkflow documentation

* refactor: update OpenSwathWorkflow test parameters for calibration settings

* refactor: update CalibrationWorkflow documentation to include debug level parameter

* refactor: remove unused quality metrics from CalibrationWorkflow

* refactor: remove unused estimateBestPeptides check in performCalibration

* doc: enhance documentation for loadMS1Map function in OpenSwathWorkflow

* refactor: update determineIrtStrategy documentation to clarify iRT strategy selection and handling of NULL_TRANSFORMATION

* refactor: separate OpenSwathWorkflowCalibration logic into reusable CalibrationWorkflow class

* refactor: remove unnecessary whitespace and comments in CalibrationWorkflow.h

commit message:
[pyOpenMS] Fix ~50 mutable reference output parameter bugs across all bindings

When C++ functions take output parameters by non-const reference
(std::vector<T>&, double&, String&), nanobind's type caster copies the
Python value into a temporary C++ object. The function modifies the
temporary, which is then discarded -- the Python caller never sees the
result. This affects all types that go through type casters (vectors,
doubles, ints, strings) but NOT nb::class_ types like MSExperiment or
ProteinIdentification, which are passed by reference correctly.

Fix pattern: remove output params from Python signature, create locals
in a lambda, call the C++ function, and return results via tuple or
direct return value. For IN/OUT params, take by value (copy) so the
C++ function can modify the copy, then return it.

Files fixed:
- bind_datastructures.cpp: DateTime (3 methods)
- bind_processing.cpp: IDFilter (4), PrecursorCorrection (3)
- bind_chemistry.cpp: ModificationDefinitionsSet, ModifiedPeptideGenerator,
  Tagger (5 methods)
- bind_format.cpp: Base64, InspectOutfile, SequestOutfile (6 methods)
- bind_ml.cpp: NonNegativeLeastSquaresSolver (2 overloads)
- bind_analysis.cpp: ConsensusMapNormalizer*, HyperScore, OPXLHelper,
  PercolatorFeatureSetHelper, SwathWindowLoader, TransformationModelLinear
  (~20 methods)
- bind_misc.cpp: AbsoluteQuantitation, Biosaur2Algorithm,
  FLASHDeconvAlgorithm, PosteriorErrorProbabilityModel, LowessSmoothing,
  PeptideIndexing, IDRipper, CsvFile, QcMLFile, and many more (~25 methods)

Also adds test_output_parameters.py regression tests (33 pass, 4 skip)
and updates test_Smoothing.py for the new smoothData() return-value API.

Full suite: 2893 passed, 0 failed.

commit message:
[pyOpenMS] Fix wheel packaging and nanobind enum abort in CI

Two CI failures fixed:

1. Wheel builds (linux, linux-arm, macOS) failed because .so files were
   missing from the wheel. The install(TARGETS) rule had COMPONENT as a
   trailing keyword which CMake silently ignored, defaulting to
   "Unspecified". When py-build-cmake ran cmake --install --component
   python_modules, only Python files were installed. Fix: specify
   COMPONENT per-type (LIBRARY/RUNTIME).

2. pyopenms_tests aborted on g++ builds with "refusing to add duplicate
   key NM_SCALE to enumeration NormalizationMethod". The unittests
   conftest.py cleared sys.modules and reimported pyopenms via
   spec_from_file_location, but nanobind's global domain state retained
   enum registrations from the first import (triggered by
   test_MRMRTNormalizer.py being collected earlier). Fix: move path
   setup to the top-level tests/conftest.py (runs before any collection)
   and never clear sys.modules for nanobind extensions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

IDA.set_data 483x, IDA.get_data 131x, getMSLevels 40x, rasterize 16x.

commit message:
[pyOpenMS] Fix Windows MSVC compilation errors in nanobind bindings

Fix three categories of pre-existing MSVC failures:

1. ParamValue type caster: use copy-initialization instead of
   static_cast for conversion operators returning by value — MSVC
   rejects static_cast for user-defined conversions to complex types

2. Replace all unsigned long with size_t in binding lambdas — on
   Windows unsigned long is 32-bit but OpenMS::Size (= size_t) is
   64-bit, causing type mismatch errors for references, containers,
   and nb::init<> template parameters

3. Replace POSIX-only std::fpos<__mbstate_t> with portable std::streampos

commit message:
Expose SpectrumRangeManager::byMSLevel() in pyOpenMS bindings

Summary: This pull request addresses issue #8751 by exposing the byMSLevel() method in the SpectrumRangeManager Cython bindings.

Changes:

Added RangeManager byMSLevel(int ms_level) except + nogil to SpectrumRangeManager.pxd.

This allows Python users to access per-MS-level range information (RT, m/z, etc.), which was previously inaccessible in pyOpenMS despite being available in the C++ core.

Use Case: Essential for tools like peak map viewers where axis ranges need to be calculated based on specific MS levels (e.g., displaying only MS1 data without interference from MS2 ranges).

commit message:
[pyOpenMS] Split MSSpectrum/MSChromatogram/MSExperiment into separate modules; fix MetaInfoInterface segfault

Split the three largest classes from bind_kernel.cpp into dedicated binding
files (bind_spectrum.cpp, bind_chromatogram.cpp, bind_experiment.cpp) for
better parallel compilation and maintainability.

Fix segfault in MetaInfoInterface methods (setMetaValue, clearMetaInfo,
isMetaEmpty) for classes with virtual destructors. When a derived class
introduces a vtable but MetaInfoInterface has none, nanobind computes
incorrect pointer offsets during base class casts. Fixed by removing
MetaInfoInterface from nanobind base declarations for CVTermList,
ChromatogramSettings, PeptideHit, PeptideIdentification, and
ProteinIdentification, using def_MetaInfoInterface<T>() helper instead.

author: Timo Sachsenberg <timo.sachsenberg@uni-tuebingen.de>
commit message:
fix: Use narrow fixed tolerance for modification mass mapping in open search

mapDeltaMassesToModifications() and generateDeltaMassStatistics() were using
the search precursor tolerance (e.g. 500 Da in open search) for matching
delta masses to known modifications. This caused every delta mass to match
the first modification found in the database ("Loss of arginine due to
transpeptidation") regardless of the actual mass shift.

Fix: use a narrow fixed tolerance (0.02 Da) for modification database lookup,
0.5 Da for cluster assignment / PSM annotation, and 0.05 Da for the near-zero
mass filter. These tolerances are intrinsic to the mapping step and must not
depend on the search precursor tolerance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Timo Sachsenberg <timo.sachsenberg@uni-tuebingen.de>
commit message:
fix: Cap modification mapping tolerance and fix unknown mod suppression

Use min(caller_tolerance, 0.02 Da) instead of raw precursor tolerance
for mapping delta masses to known modifications. This prevents overly
broad matching in open search mode (500 Da tolerance) while preserving
SageAdapter's intentional 0.01 Da tolerance. Also fix pre-existing bug
where unknown modifications were suppressed by a zero-threshold check
on the unmatched mod_mass (which stayed 0.0). Add test coverage for
artificial unknown delta mass (123.456 Da) in both C++ and Python tests.

commit message:
feat: Expand fragment index open search with modification discovery and FDR filtering (#8414)

* feat: Expand fragment index open search for modification discovery

This commit enhances the fragment index-based search algorithm with
comprehensive modification discovery capabilities:

New Data Structures in OpenSearchModificationAnalysis:
- DeltaMassEntry: Statistics for delta mass histogram bins
- PTMEntry: Mapped PTM statistics with residue localization
- DeltaMassStatistics: Container for delta mass table
- PTMStatistics: Container for PTM table with residue analysis
- OpenSearchAnalysisResult: Combined result structure

New Methods:
- analyzeModificationsWithStatistics(): Main entry point for
  modification discovery, returns structured statistics tables
- generateDeltaMassStatistics(): Generates delta mass histogram table
- generatePTMStatistics(): Generates PTM table with residue analysis
- analyzeResidueFrequency(): Analyzes amino acid frequencies per delta mass
- writeDeltaMassStatistics(): Writes delta mass TSV output
- writePTMStatistics(): Writes PTM TSV output
- Helper methods for modification database lookup

PeptideSearchEngineFIAlgorithm enhancements:
- New SearchResult struct with modification analysis results
- New searchWithModificationAnalysis() method that returns
  comprehensive results including PTM and delta mass tables
- Enhanced logging with formatted tables of top PTMs and
  unknown delta masses for potential novel modification discovery

The modification analysis functionality is factored out into
OpenSearchModificationAnalysis class following DRY principles,
allowing both SageAdapter and the FI algorithm to share the code.

Output files generated:
- *_DeltaMassStats.tsv: Delta mass histogram with mapping status
- *_PTMStats.tsv: Mapped PTMs with residue frequency analysis

* feat: Add Python bindings for modification analysis classes

Add pyOpenMS wrappers for the new modification analysis functionality:

OpenSearchModificationAnalysis.pxd:
- Full Python binding for OpenSearchModificationAnalysis class
- Wrapped all new structs: DeltaMassEntry, PTMEntry,
  DeltaMassStatistics, PTMStatistics, OpenSearchAnalysisResult
- Wrapped all analysis methods including analyzeModificationsWithStatistics()
- Added comprehensive docstrings with usage examples

PeptideSearchEngineFIAlgorithm.pxd:
- Added import for OpenSearchModificationAnalysis
- Added SearchResult struct wrapping
- Added searchWithModificationAnalysis() method binding
- Updated documentation with open search modification discovery example

Both classes now provide complete Python API access for:
- Delta mass histogram analysis
- PTM mapping to known modifications
- Residue frequency analysis for localization

refactor: Make FeatureFinderMultiplexAlgorithm::run() take const MSExperiment&

caller's experiment via swap(), sortSpectra(), getChromatograms().clear(),

internal MS1 filtering so callers passing mixed-level data (like

commit message:
Split monolithic OpenMS library into Core, IO, and Algo sub-libraries

Decompose the single libOpenMS.so into three shared libraries to improve
incremental build times and enforce cleaner dependency boundaries:

- OpenMS_Core (8 MB): KERNEL, CONCEPT, SYSTEM, MATH, DATASTRUCTURES,
  METADATA, CHEMISTRY, IONMOBILITY — fundamental data structures
- OpenMS_IO (35 MB): FORMAT — file format readers/writers
- OpenMS_Algo (20 MB): ML, ANALYSIS, PROCESSING, FEATUREFINDER,
  COMPARISON, QC, APPLICATIONS — algorithms and analysis

Key design decisions:
- Use include() instead of add_subdirectory() to preserve
  CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR for existing sources.cmake relative paths
- Hand-crafted OpenMSConfig.h replaces auto-generated export header
  to support multiple library export macros
- INTERFACE umbrella target "OpenMS" maintains backward compatibility
- LINK_GROUP:RESCAN handles remaining Core→IO back-dependencies
  (File.cpp, ModificationsDB.cpp, DocumentIdentifier.cpp,
  ProteinIdentification.cpp reference FORMAT types)
- Six leaf files moved from Core to IO/Algo to minimize circular deps
- CXX_VISIBILITY_PRESET=default for Phase 1 cross-library compatibility

All 2455 tests pass (9 pre-existing external tool failures unchanged).

Add MSVC monolithic fallback and restore LINK_GROUP:RESCAN

Windows DLLs require all symbols resolved at link time with proper

  IO→Algo back-dependencies (--as-needed was dropping Algo from link)

commit message:
Use --no-as-needed for split sub-libraries to fix test linking

Replace LINK_GROUP:RESCAN with a custom NO_AS_NEEDED link group that
wraps the three sub-libraries in --no-as-needed / --as-needed flags.

This solves two problems:
1. IO→Algo back-dependency linker errors: --as-needed was dropping Algo
   from the link when the consumer didn't directly reference Algo symbols,
   causing IO's Algo references to be unresolved.
2. Empty Core singletons (ModificationsDB, ProteaseDB, RNaseDB): IO
   registers populators via static initializers that only run when the
   .so is loaded. Without --no-as-needed, IO was dropped from DT_NEEDED
   and its initializers never ran, causing tutorials to crash with
   "Modification not found: Oxidation".

LINK_GROUP:RESCAN (--start-group/--end-group) didn't solve problem #2
and isn't supported by Apple ld.  --no-as-needed handles both issues
and the NO_AS_NEEDED link group definition is set at the top-level
CMakeLists.txt so all consuming directories inherit it.

macOS uses plain link order with -undefined dynamic_lookup on each
sub-library (no --as-needed behavior on macOS).
